prior_art_found: Serious and RECENT. (1) van Roestel et al. 2026, arXiv:2609.08923 — posted ~2 weeks before this gate — is the same physics channel executed with a strictly better instrument. I fetched the paper HTML: they queried Kowalski for all alerts within 3" of a 273,000-object Gaia WD candidate catalogue, got 602,926 alerts across 26,466 WDs, visually inspected the 4,027 WDs with >=3 NEGATIVE alerts, vetted to 19 objects of interest, confirmed 6 deep obscurations (25-100%, weeks to years) plus 3 candidate debris hosts. They state the junk is "cataclysmic variables, image artefacts, or high proper motion stars" — precisely the lane's veto list. Note: the paper does NOT itself claim methodological novelty and does NOT propose a field-star extension (a search-engine paraphrase asserted it does; the HTML does not) — but a ZTF-variability group with spectroscopic access has now demonstrated the channel end-to-end and has every incentive to widen the parent catalogue. (2) Tzanidakis & Davenport 2025, arXiv:2508.03964 / ApJ (main-sequence dippers in ZTF) and arXiv:2507.19594 (ASAS-SN big dippers) work the detected-dip regime. scooped_fraction_estimate: ~40-60% of the realistic yield space is already worked, rising fast. By class: white dwarfs — effectively fully scooped by van Roestel 2026 (though mostly at G>18.5, i.e. mostly fainter than this lane's parent window, so the OBJECT overlap is small; the METHOD overlap is total). VY Scl / polars — partially worked (Duffy 2024, Szkody, PolarCat, ZTF Source Classification Project) and these are the dominant deep-fade population surviving the |b|>5-10 cut. RCB/DY Per — heavily and continuously mined by Tisserand/Karambelkar with WISE-colour preselection, and the latitude cut removes the disk/bulge reservoir where most live. UXor — young stars, |b|<10, cut away. Long-eclipse giants (Gaia17bpp class) — ~3 known objects total in history; the claim of "10-40 new" in the bright tier is the least defensible number in the proposal. Genuinely untouched residue = high-latitude non-WD, non-catalogued-CV deep faders, which is exactly the population whose surface density the project already measured as small.
why_not_done_claim_credible: Half honest, half self-serving, and one pillar is factually wrong. HONEST: ZTF DRs really do publish detections only; Tzanidakis & Davenport really do require >=50 detections per filter, which structurally excludes fully-censored fades; Duffy 2024 really does say it could not measure lows in gaps; and the stated distinction from the project's own CLOSED bimodal state-cycler lane (that lane required both states detected) is real and correctly argued, not a recycle. WRONG: "brokers drop negative-flux alerts." They do not. ALeRCE, Lasair and Fink all carry isdiffpos='f' candidates, and van Roestel 2026 is built entirely on ZTF negative alerts from Kowalski — the proposal's OWN data_sources list "ALeRCE public API (isdiffpos-negative alerts)", contradicting its own why-not-done in the same document. SELF-SERVING: "the per-frame polygons and limits live in a separate metadata table nobody joins." ztf_current_meta_sci exists precisely so people can join it, and more importantly ZTF Forced Photometry (ZFPS) returns actual per-epoch flux at any position — a strictly stronger measurement than an absence statistic, and the standard professional tool. The lane's claim to an untouched lever survives only if you ignore both negative alerts and forced photometry, which are the two instruments a professional would reach for first and which this project has itself used. Also note levers #2 and #3 of the project's own verified list (reference-seeding invisibility; pre-reference turn-on produces no alerts) DO NOT BIND HERE — the parent sample is defined by ngoodobs>=100 and |refmag-medianmag|<0.5, i.e. every target is in the reference and therefore does generate negative alerts. The lane borrows credibility from levers that do not apply to it.
depth_arithmetic: DEPTH: ZTF public r 5-sigma per-frame limit is ~20.5-20.8. For a non-detection to be unambiguous you need the source ~0.5 mag below the frame limit, r>21.0. Parent r=18.5 must fade 2.5 mag; r=17.5 must fade 3.5 mag; r=16.0 must fade 5.0 mag. The N4 bright tier ("3 mag below the per-frame limit", r>23.5, sustained >=3 yr) demands a 6.0 mag fade at r=17.5 and 7.5 mag at r=16.0 held for three years. Objects that do that: RCB stars (yes, 6-8 mag declines — but ~150 Galactic known, disk/bulge concentrated, and the |b|>5-10 cut deletes the reservoir) and essentially nothing else except ~3 historical Gaia17bpp-class objects. "Bright tier 15-150 raw, 10-40 new" is not supported by any known population. COVERAGE: ~22,000 deg^2, ~115k quadrants, ~2e7 parent objects at |b|>10 — fine, ZTF covers it. FALSE-POSITIVE ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS THE REAL PROBLEM: the pilot's 0/3,000 catalogue-level survivors bounds the residual post-veto false rate at only <1.0e-3 (rule of three, 95%). Over 2e7 parent objects that bound permits up to ~20,000 false survivors — two orders of magnitude above the claimed 200-400 real post-control flags. To bound the false rate tightly enough that false survivors stay under ~40 you need <2e-6 per source, which requires ~1.5 MILLION control sources with zero survivors. The pilot is 500x short of the control volume its own conclusion requires. YIELD CROSS-CHECK: the project's own closed bimodal state-cycler lane measured <0.01 deg^-2, i.e. <220 systems over 22,000 deg^2 for states that ARE detected. A fully-censored state requires a strictly DEEPER fade than a detected one, so the censored population should be rarer, not equal. The proposal's "~300 fully censored state-cyclers at |b|>10" silently assumes censored >= detected with no physical or empirical support. SCALE CROSS-CHECK vs van Roestel: they visually inspected 1.5% of their parent (4,027/273,000) and converted 0.15% of inspections into confirmations. The same inspection fraction on a 2e7 parent is ~295,000 objects to eyeball. Even the lane's own stricter trigger (>=8 consecutive frames over >=5 nights) is an unvalidated guess at how far that comes down.
access_ok: Yes, cleanly — this is the lane's strongest leg. ZTF DR24 HATS light curves and objects are public on AWS S3 anonymously (s3://ipac-irsa-ztf/ztf/enhanced/dr24/{lc,objects}/hats; HATS release announced 2026-05-26, DR24 itself 2026-01-22), with an IRSA tutorial for exactly this access pattern and a per-file HTTP mirror at irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/download/parquet/ztf/dr24/lc/hats/. That routes entirely around verified lever #4 (the ~1,100-query per-position API rate limit that returns empty 200s) — the design correctly forbids the per-position API and uses the HATS object-ID index. ztf_current_meta_sci (61.3M quadrant rows: obsjd, corner polygons, maglimit, seeing, infobits, programid) and ztf_current_meta_ref are public via IRSA TAP; ~1,185 per-field pulls at ~35 s is ~12 h single-threaded, fine. Gaia DR3 HATS, GALEX, LS DR10 forced unWISE all public. RISKS, not blockers: (a) 50-100 GB of column-projected parquet plus intermediates on a 6-core box — disk headroom is unverified and enzo is a shared-host guest, so this is a real operational constraint, not a rounding error; (b) the Lasair "live twin" is shaky — per project memory the ZTF token 401s on lasair.lsst.ac.uk and filter/watchlist creation is UI-only, and the user cannot register new accounts; treat the live twin as optional garnish, not a deliverable; (c) ALeRCE negative-alert corroboration is available and should be promoted from "corroboration" to a primary screen, since it is the same signal measured better.
cheapest_kill_test: Run the visit-deficit statistic, with the FULL veto stack and the exact production configuration, on a known-positive panel of ~19 positions and require >=9/11 recovery BEFORE any parent-sample run: van Roestel 2026's 6 confirmed WD obscurations (arXiv:2609.08923, incl. ZTF J2327+0019 which vanished >1 yr), Duffy 2024's 8 VY Scl systems at their documented low-state epochs, and ~5 AAVSO-documented post-2019 RCB declines. This is ~19 cone lookups plus the per-quadrant metadata join — one to two days, no sky-wide compute, no new accounts. It is decisive in both directions: if the statistic cannot re-find events that are PUBLISHED, spectroscopically confirmed and multi-magnitude deep, the lane is dead on the spot; if it recovers them, you have simultaneously satisfied verified lever #7 (template recovery on the pipeline's own configuration) and produced the depth-vs-gap-length recovery curve the yield model currently lacks. Pair it with a same-day negative-alert cross-check: pull ALeRCE isdiffpos='f' alerts at those same 19 positions. If negative alerts flag the events and the deficit statistic adds nothing, the correct lane is not this one — it is the negative-alert search on a non-WD parent, which is cheaper, better-conditioned, and the thing van Roestel will do next. Do NOT spend the 500x control-volume expansion (~1.5M clean controls needed to bound the false rate) until this 19-object panel passes.
biggest_risk: The false-positive floor is unmeasured at the scale that decides the lane, and the pilot's own numbers say so: 0/3,000 bounds the residual rate only at <1e-3, which over 2e7 objects permits ~20,000 false survivors against a claimed ~200-400 real ones. This is the closed turn-on lane's structural lesson wearing new clothes — an absence-vs-expectation comparison is definitionally satisfied by every pipeline pathology (bad-pixel masks, bright-neighbour halos, catflags, seeing-dependent blending, association-radius edge cases), and the pilot has so far identified exactly ONE artifact class (edge jitter, 97% of the naive tail). Finding one artifact class and vetoing it is not evidence there is no second. Second risk, close behind: a professional group with spectroscopic follow-up published the same physics channel via a strictly superior instrument two weeks ago, so the 12-18 month window is optimistic, and the sample where this lane's statistic beats negative alerts is empty by construction (every parent object is in the reference and therefore alerting).
one_line_reason: Real unworked statistic, public data, working VSX credit channel and an honest non-recycle argument — but the yield model contradicts the project's own measured <0.01 deg^-2 density, the latitude cut deletes the RCB and UXor reservoirs that supply the deep fades, one why-not-done pillar ("brokers drop negative alerts") is simply false and refuted by the lane's own data_sources and by van Roestel 2026, and the pilot's control volume is 500x too small to bound the false-positive rate at the scale required; it is worth exactly the two-day 19-object recovery panel and nothing more until that passes.

scooped_fraction_estimate: Registry-wise ~0% scooped: no DR-based catalogue covers 2023-03-09 to 2025-10-22, and essentially none of the expected events are in VSX or TNS. Candidate-list-wise I estimate 25-45% of the bright (r<20, amplitude>0.5) in-window events already carry a Fink microlensing-module or ALeRCE microlensing-class tag, and a few percent carry a TNS AT name from broker auto-reporting. The censored-faint-baseline tail is ~0% present in any DR catalogue (excluded by construction by the >=30-point rule) but probably >50% present as untagged or mis-tagged alerts. Paper-scoop clock: DR25 lands 2027-01-20 and will hand the incumbents both the 2025-10-22 to 2026-10 window and the plane partnership data through ~mid-2025; assume a Caltech DR2x sequel paper within 6-15 months, which removes the publication claim but not VSX filings made first.
why_not_done_claim_credible: Mostly credible, with one self-serving sentence that matters. Credible: the DR-lag arithmetic is exact and verifiable (DR24 released 2026-01-22 covering to 2025-10-22; only two DR catalogues exist, the latest ending 2023-03-09); Gaia Science Alerts really ended 2025-01-15; the >=30-point rule really does exclude censored-faint baselines by construction; OGLE-IV really is bulge-only. Self-serving: "Fink's module tags candidates but nobody files them" is the lane quietly admitting that a public machine-made candidate list already exists for a large slice of the yield — i.e. that slice is propagation labor, the category the user shelved outright (GFCAT/GSA/EXOD/SSOLS). The lane's own funnel then makes that slice STEP ONE. The defence is that a broker class is an impure bucket rather than a curated list, so separating real events from thousands of DN/YSO/AGN contaminants is genuine vetting, not transcription — but the lane should have said so instead of blurring it. Second overreach: the two "tails" sold as the unique contribution are the two weakest. A censored baseline means fs, u0 and tE are degenerate, so the very events the lane claims no one has admitted are the ones on which a PSPL fit cannot be defended, and the Galactic-plane faint-baseline single-outburst population is dominated by rare-outburst dwarf novae. And the tE>=250 d tail is partly pre-empted by Rodriguez+2022's published 1,558 "level ongoing" candidates, while its headline payoff (black-hole lens mass via parallax) is telescope-gated in substance.
depth_arithmetic: Window: Zhai+2024 ends 2023-03-09; DR24 ends 2025-10-22 (MJD 60970, matches the lane's number exactly). Gap = 2.62 yr, entirely uncatalogued. Rate: Rodriguez 60 events/3.0 yr = 20/yr on Phase-I public cadence; Zhai 124/5.0 yr = 24.8/yr with high-cadence plane fields folded in. Naive yield 2.62 x 20-25 = 52-65 events, so the lane's "60-90" is 15-30% optimistic but the right order. Cadence correction the lane glosses: DR24's proprietary cutoff is 550 d before release = 2024-07-22, so for the final 1.25 yr of the window only the public 2-day g/r survey is present, not the ~196 high-cadence rr plane fields Zhai leaned on. Using Rodriguez's public-cadence rate for that 1.25 yr: 1.37 x 25 + 1.25 x 20 = 34 + 25 = ~59. Post-Gaia sub-window (2025-01-15 to 2025-10-22 = 0.77 yr, public cadence only) gives 0.77 x 20 = ~15 events with no Gaia name, not the claimed 30-40 — that specific claim is roughly 2x inflated. Depth: ZTF public 30 s exposures reach r ~20.5-20.8 (5-sigma), g ~20.8; Zhai's sources sit at r 14-20. A baseline at r 20.5-21.5 is below the single-epoch limit by construction, which is exactly why detection-censoring is real (lever 1) and exactly why those events are unfittable. Sky/volume: plane strip |b|<20, dec>-28 is ~30-35% of sky by area but holds the majority of ZTF's 5.32e9 light curves; a full light-curve HATS pass is multi-TB and not sane on a 6-core box over a home link. Feasible route is the DR24 HATS Objects table (one collapsed-metrics row per object) for the max-minus-median pre-cut, then pulling light curves only for the ~1e4-1e5 survivors. Long-tE tail: Zhai's longest was 421 d; a tE>=250 d cut over a 7.6-yr baseline plausibly yields 2-6 events, but each is a multi-year smooth symmetric brightening, i.e. photometrically degenerate with LPV maxima, UXors and slow accretors, and Rodriguez already published 1,558 ongoing-long candidates. Control exists and is decisive: re-run the pipeline on DR24 restricted to the DR17 epoch range and recover Zhai's 124.
access_ok: Yes. ZTF DR24 is public now: released 2026-01-22, span 2018-03-01 to 2025-10-22, 5.32e9 light curves, and the DR24 HATS Lightcurves + Objects catalogs have been available at IRSA since 2026-05-26 (caltech-ipac.github.io/irsa-tutorials/ztf-lightcurves). ZTF is also on the AWS Registry of Open Data, so bulk parquet/S3 access bypasses the per-position IRSA API entirely — this lane never has to touch the ~1,100-query empty-200 rate limit (lever 4), which is the single best access property it has. Fink has a public REST API (no account needed) for the microlensing-module class; ALeRCE has a public API. Gaia DR3, PS1 DR2, LS DR10 (incl. forced unWISE W1/W2, lever 5) all queryable without registration. OGLE-IV EWS event lists are public static pages. VSX cone search is public and the user's VSX account is live, so the credit channel needs no new registration. Only TNS submission needs task #152, and it is optional here. Compute: the Objects-table pre-cut is the only tractable entry point on 6 cores; a blind full-light-curve scan of the plane is not.
cheapest_kill_test: One day, two API loops, no pipeline. Take Zhai+2024's published 124 high-confidence events (machine-readable table) and, for each: (a) VSX cone search at 3 arcsec — how many are already in VSX? (b) Fink and ALeRCE object queries — how many carry a microlensing tag/class? (c) TNS cone — how many have an AT name? This measures both gates at once on a ground-truth sample. Kill conditions: if (a) is high, the VSX filing niche is already being worked and the credit channel is gone; if (b) is high (say >60% recovered by the Fink module), then the in-window events are already sitting on a public machine-made list and the lane is propagation labor wearing a discovery hat — NO_GO by the user's own shelving rule. Proceed only if VSX recall is ~0 AND broker recall is low or the broker class is demonstrably swamped (measure the class's raw population in the same plane fields: if Fink's microlensing class returns thousands of objects for 2023-2025 against an expected ~60 real events, the tag is a bucket, not a list, and separating them is real work). Do this BEFORE the DR24 funnel build. Second, non-negotiable, gate (lever 7): recover Zhai's 124 from DR24 restricted to DR17 epochs on your own configuration before any yield or absence claim.
biggest_risk: That the yield is real but unfilable at scale. Two compounding failure modes: (1) Discovery-vs-propagation — a large, unmeasured fraction of the bright in-window events already carry public Fink/ALeRCE microlensing tags, so the lane risks being the shelved orphan-worklist pattern with a new coat of paint; the lane's own funnel starts there, which is a tell. (2) Classification defensibility — the deliverable is a TYPE CLAIM, not an object detection, and the referee is a VSX moderator. Achromatic-symmetric-single-episode on sparse 2-day g/r photometry is Zhai's own criterion, but Zhai still had to call 54/178 merely "possible" with a full pipeline and detection-efficiency simulations. An amateur filing ~50 MICROLENS classifications will hit dwarf-nova/WZ Sge contamination hard in the plane, and the censored-faint tail — the lane's claimed unique population — is precisely where blending degeneracy makes the PSPL fit unfalsifiable. Realistic throughput at 2-4 h/event vetting plus moderation round-trips is months, not the advertised weeks, and a batch of rejected or later-overturned MICROLENS entries would cost the user standing in the one credit channel they have.
one_line_reason: A genuinely empty, precisely-bounded 2.62-yr catalogue window (2023-03-09 to 2025-10-22) in fully public DR24 data, with a live no-telescope credit channel and a hard self-recovery control — but it stays a candidate, not a GO, until the one-day broker-overlap test proves the events are not already sitting on Fink's and ALeRCE's public microlensing lists, and the scope is cut to the bright fittable core (drop the censored-faint tail's type claims and the telescope-gated black-hole framing).

scooped_fraction_estimate: North branch ~85-95% scooped: same parent sample, a strictly more sensitive absence detector already run and published 12 days ago, in the hands of the named confirmer. South branch ~20-30% scooped as a method (no DES pair-drop search found), but ~90% of its realistic yield is deep Algols/CVs rather than the WD systems the title sells. Weighted over the merged lane as written (where north carries most of the labour and essentially all of the claimed 30-80 yield): ~75-85%.
why_not_done_claim_credible: Half honest, half self-serving, and it contradicts itself. HONEST: prior BLS searches genuinely require in-eclipse detections - van Roestel+2021 demanded >=5 in-transit points, and ZTFJ0038+2030 got the WRONG period from only 4. That gap is real. SELF-SERVING AND REFUTED: (1) It claims the pros are blocked because "ZFPS at 1e5 positions is impractical" - but the lane's own funnel only needs ZFPS on <=200 objects, so by its own design the barrier it names is not the barrier. (2) It claims "a missing-epoch statistic joined to the exposure table is engineering, not a paper topic" - van Roestel+2026 just published exactly an absence-statistic paper on exactly this parent sample, so the premise is false on the record. (3) It claims "the rational group move is to wait" for Rubin - refuted by four 2026 papers on this population (2609.08923, 2608.19493, 2606.03850, 2606.03737). The field is hot and professionally instrumented right now, which is the opposite of the solo-amateur criterion. (4) The southern justification leans on "DES stellar-variability work modelled RR Lyrae, never pair-drops" - that one I could not disprove and it is the lane's single credible unworked claim.
depth_arithmetic:
NORTH - the p_i cut and the miss requirement are in a vise the lane never notices. ZTF median 5-sigma single-frame limit is r ~ 20.5 (van Roestel+2026, verbatim: "a median limiting magnitude of ~20.5 AB-mag in 30 s"). The lane requires p_i > 0.98, which needs SNR >~ 8-10, i.e. quiescent mag <~ limmag - 0.75 ~ 19.75. A "miss" simultaneously requires eclipse depth > headroom (limmag - mag). So: at G = 20.3 the headroom is 0.2 mag (a shallow eclipse makes a miss) but p_i > 0.98 FAILS and the epoch is discarded; at G = 18.5 p_i > 0.98 passes but you now need depth > 2.0 mag. The usable window is G ~ 18.5-19.7 requiring depths 0.8-2.0 mag - NOT the advertised G 18.5-20.8. That is roughly 70k targets, not 140k + 50k = 200k, and it sits squarely inside the magnitude range van Roestel+2021, Brown+2023 and Rebassa+2025 already BLS-searched.

NORTH - the population is in the wrong place. Total eclipses come from WD+dM, but a WD with a detectable M companion is pushed OFF the P_WD > 0.75 locus into the bridge - and the bridge is precisely Rebassa-Mansergas+2025's sample (920 ZTF-accessible, 63 eclipsers, ~50% complete by their own estimate). What remains ON the locus is WD+late-M/BD (a literal handful known: ZTFJ0038+2030, J0404+1112) and double WDs, whose eclipses are typically < 1 mag because the two components are comparable - so DWDs produce no misses at all. The claimed "300-1,000 eclipsers in the bin" and "30-80 confirmed" is unsupported; single digits is the defensible number.

NORTH - the statistics are off by orders of magnitude. Eclipse duty cycle for P = 0.1-2 d WD binaries is ~1-3%, so 300-500 frames give 3-15 true in-eclipse misses - and the lane's own threshold is >=6. Meanwhile ZTF DR light curves carry ~1-5% spurious non-detections for well-measured sources (chip gaps, masking, trails, deblend failures, catflags, astrometric mismatch) = 10-20 instrumental misses per object, i.e. MORE background than signal. Those misses are not independent: they cluster by night, field, quadrant, moon phase and season, which is structured at exactly the 1-day and sub-day aliases where P = 0.04-2 d binaries live. The stated ">4 sigma vs shuffled epochs" is wrong twice: 2e5 objects x ~1e5 trial periods = ~1e10 trials needs far more than 4 sigma, and shuffling epochs destroys the very correlated structure that generates the false positives, so it tests the wrong null.

SOUTH - the arithmetic here actually works, and this is the only sound part. DES 90 s single-epoch depth is r ~ 23.4, so a source at r = 20-21.5 dropping >=1.2 mag lands at r = 21.2-22.7, still detected at SNR ~ 10-30. This is a MEASURED drop, not a non-detection - far more robust than the north branch. But the yield is oversold: with mean ndetr = 9.7 and ~40 total griz epochs = ~20 pairs, at 2% duty cycle and a ~5.8 min eclipse vs 2.0 min pair separation, P(at least one pair fully in eclipse) = 20 x 0.02 x 0.65 ~ 23%, not the claimed 60-85% x 50-70%. Of 50-150 eclipsers that is ~12-35 pair-corroborated, and the lane itself concedes the composition: "0-3 double-WD/WD+BD and hundreds of deep Algols". Also, the two exposures of a DES pair are in DIFFERENT filters, so "drops by >=1.2 mag in both" must be measured per-band against a ~10-point baseline, which the lane never states. And one pair of in-eclipse points yields NO period, while VSX EA wants one.
access_ok: Mostly yes, with one caveat the lane hides. ZTF DR24 bulk HATS/S3 sidesteps the ~1,100-query IRSA per-position rate limit (verified lever 4) and IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_sci gives the frame metadata - fine. ZFPS is bound to the existing TU Delft account, batches <=1,500, <=200 finalists - fine, no new account needed. NSC DR2 via anonymous Data Lab TAP is empirically proven by this project's own closed turn-on lane (9,745 objects processed), so tiled queries work. CAVEAT: nsc_dr2.meas across the full 5,000 deg2 DES footprint at r = 20-21.5 is ~10-25 million objects x ~40 measurement rows = 4e8-1e9 rows. That is not pullable through anonymous TAP without an aggressive colour pre-cut on nsc_dr2.object first (the lane implies one via "WD density 10-25 deg^-2" but never states it), and anonymous access has no mydb for staging. Feasible in tiles, but the lane's stated 2 weeks for the south assumes an ingest it has not sized. Compute: per-frame p_i calibration on the 200 nearest reference sources per quadrant-epoch for 200k objects x >=300 frames, plus a dense-grid binary BLS over 0.04-2 d, on a 6-core box, is weeks of wall clock on its own.
cheapest_kill_test: One afternoon, no new data, kills the north branch (which carries most of the labour and all of the claimed yield) before a single 200k-object run. Take the ~10-30 KNOWN total/deep eclipsing WD binaries at G 18.5-19.7 inside the ZTF footprint from van Roestel+2021, the 2022 "four deeply eclipsing WDs" paper, Brown+2023 and Rebassa+2025. Pull their ZTF DR24 light curves plus the ztf_current_meta_sci frame list at their positions and answer two questions: (a) SELF-RECOVERY (lever 7) - does the exact intended pipeline, on its own configuration, produce a >4-sigma phase-coherent miss signal at each object's KNOWN published period? (b) NULL RATE - for ~1,000 magnitude-matched NON-variable Gaia WDs, what is the distribution of "impossible misses" (p_i > 0.98, no row) per object, and what fraction already clear the >=6-miss trigger? KILL CONDITIONS: control recovery below ~50%, OR more than ~5% of non-variable controls reaching >=6 impossible misses, OR the recovered control periods showing 1-day-alias structure. Any one of those means the signal is below the instrumental floor and the lane dies on arithmetic rather than after five weeks of pipeline work. Run (b) BEFORE (a) - it is a pure counting job and it is the one most likely to fire.
biggest_risk: The north branch is a weaker reimplementation of a search published 12 days ago on the identical 273k-WD parent sample, by the very person named as the community confirmer - and the lane's own stated hard gate ("show from their selection rules that minute-scale periodic dropouts were excluded") resolves AGAINST it, since van Roestel+2026 excluded only KNOWN periodic variables and inspected 4,027 WDs with >=3 negative alerts. Underneath that sits the structural repeat of the CLOSED turn-on lane: ~3-15 true in-eclipse misses buried in ~10-20 instrumental misses that are correlated on exactly the nightly/sidereal timescales the target periods occupy, so the detection criterion is satisfied by artifacts definitionally - the same failure mode, on a new object class, unaddressed.
one_line_reason: The lane's own hard gate fires against it - van Roestel+2026 (arXiv:2609.08923, 12 days old) already ran a strictly more sensitive absence search on the identical 273k Gaia-WD parent and excluded only KNOWN periodic variables - while the p_i>0.98 cut collapses the usable window to the already-BLS-searched G 18.5-19.7, the total-eclipse population (WD+dM) sits off the P_WD>0.75 locus in Rebassa+2025's bridge, and the 3-15 true in-eclipse misses are outnumbered by nightly-correlated instrumental misses in a repeat of the closed turn-on lane; the one sound piece, the DES back-to-back filter-pair drop, is unscooped but delivers periodless deep Algols, which is bookkeeping, not novelty.

prior_art_found:
THE LANE'S OWN BLIND SPOT, and it is the dominant threat: Gaia Photometric Science Alerts (GSA). Hodgkin et al. 2021 (A&A 652, A76) states GSA explicitly detects "Gaia sources which have undergone a significant brightening OR FADING", all-sky at sub-arcsecond resolution INCLUDING the plane and bulge, continuously since 2014 — i.e. the same instrument, the same photons, the same 2014-2020 window, the same signal, running in real time for 12 years, with every detection published immediately under a Gaia14xxx-Gaia26xxx name. Gaia17bpp (arXiv:2306.12409; the deepest and longest known dimming event, a 4.5 mag disk occultation) is a GSA discovery. Gaia-GIC-1 (2026, ApJL) likewise. The lane's 3,000-word rationale never mentions GSA once. That omission is disqualifying for the "why hasn't someone done this" claim as written.

What GSA does NOT cover, and this is why the lane is not dead: external completeness is only C_E = 0.46 (scanning-law + both-FOV requirement), there is a documented bias toward BRIGHTENING events (faint systems only become visible when they brighten), and the source must already be in the internal catalogue. So a residual faint-end/threshold-missed population genuinely exists.

Supply-side prior art, real and directly comparable: JoHantgen, Rowan, Forés-Toribio, Kochanek, Stanek, Shappee, Dong, Prieto, Thompson 2025, "A Systematic Search for Big Dippers in ASAS-SN" (arXiv:2507.19594, A&A accepted) — 5.1M targets searched, 12 found in normal ops + 4 new candidates = 16 total. This is the rate calibrator and it is the correct one; the lane cites it honestly. Also arXiv:2508.03964 (systematic main-sequence dipper search) and ASASSN-24fw (arXiv:2507.03080).

DR4 contents VERIFIED against the ESA DR4 content page: release 2 Dec 2026, 2.8G sources, 66 months (25 Jul 2014 - 20 Jan 2020), ~400 TB, epoch photometry 121,845,163,512 rows. gaiadr4.vari_summary at exactly 403,061,676 rows — the lane's number is CORRECT, not invented. vari_eclipsing_binary 2,392,500; vari_short_timescale 8,386,659; vari_long_period_variable 4,437,454; vari_rotation_modulation 18,237,848; new-in-DR4 vari_flaring_star 89,355 and vari_pms_oscillator 323; plus microlensing, planetary transits, compact-companion candidates. CONFIRMED: there is NO single-dip / one-off-fading table in the DR4 contents list. The lane's central structural claim holds.

gaiadr3.vari_summary column check (ESA DR3 data model): it is a full statistics table, not a pointer table — per-band min/max/mean/median mag, range, trimmed range, std dev, SKEWNESS, kurtosis, MAD, IQR, Abbe, Stetson, num_selected_g_fov, time_duration_g_fov. Stage 1 as specified is technically executable IF DR4 keeps the schema (ESA's DR4 one-liner describes vari_summary only as "information on where a source can be found in the different Variability tables", which is ambiguous — unverified risk).

No published Gaia-epoch-photometry single-dip/one-off-eclipse mining paper found after 10 searches. Nearest neighbours are all period-based (2.2M DR3 EB candidates), YSO-variability, WD-variability, hot-subdwarf ML, and AGN-variability searches on DR3 epoch photometry.

scooped_fraction_estimate: 60-75% of the theoretical yield is already taken or will be taken within weeks. Breakdown: (a) GSA has been harvesting the G<19 bright half of this exact signal in real time since 2014 at ~46% external completeness — call it 40-50% of the all-sky detectable population already named and credited; (b) OGLE-IV (~3,000 deg^2 southern disk + ~600 deg^2 bulge, I<21, hours-to-days cadence, 2010-2020) plus VVV/VVVX (~560 deg^2) cover the densest part of the claimed southern window with vastly better sampling — another ~10-15%; (c) DPAC has had DR4 internally for years and publishes simultaneously with the release, and the external day-1 community (Tzanidakis/Davenport, SNAD, ALeRCE, ASAS-SN group, the Cambridge GSA team) all have DR3-column pipelines already written — a skewness + (median-min) cut on vari_summary is among the two or three most obvious queries anyone writes on 2 Dec, so the claimed 1-3 month window is realistically days to ~2 weeks for the obvious cuts. Residual genuinely-open surface: the G~18-19 slice at dec<-30 outside the OGLE/VVV footprints, and GSA threshold-misses. That is real but it is tens of objects, not the 100-200 claimed.
why_not_done_claim_credible:
MIXED — one half verifiably true, the other half self-serving, plus one disqualifying omission.

TRUE AND VERIFIED: "no dip table is in the DR4 contents list" — I checked the ESA DR4 content page against all 20 variability tables and there is no single-dip/one-off-fading product. CU7's eclipsing-binary pipeline is Lomb-Scargle + multi-harmonic Fourier, structurally incapable of emitting an unrepeated event; the published CU7 EB detection rate (89%) is measured on PERIODIC sources. The structural gap is real.

SELF-SERVING: "Their constraint is priority, not capability; the amateur's edge is ... willingness." This cuts the wrong way. A TAP query on a statistics table is cheap precisely BECAUSE it takes no priority to run. Low capability cost means low protection. The lane converts the query's own cheapness into a moat, which is backwards. And "El-Badry-type groups will spend the first months on NSS/astrometric binaries" is a guess about specific named researchers' Q1-2027 priorities, offered as if it were a fact.

DISQUALIFYING OMISSION: the lane never mentions Gaia Photometric Science Alerts. Gaia has been running a real-time all-sky fading-event detector on these exact photons since 2014, publishing every catch with a name. Any honest "why hasn't someone done this" for a Gaia single-dip search must open with GSA and then argue the residual — GSA's 0.46 external completeness, its brightening bias, its internal-catalogue requirement. That argument is winnable. The lane did not make it, which means either the lane was constructed without checking its own instrument's alert stream, or it checked and left it out. Either way the stated rationale cannot be trusted as written and the yield estimate inherits that error.

Note also: GSA sits in this project's own closed-lane ledger as SHELVED (orphan worklists GFCAT/GSA/EXOD). The lane is adjacent to a shelved lane and does not say so.
depth_arithmetic:
SAMPLING. DR4 span 2010 d (25 Jul 2014 - 20 Jan 2020). DR3 (34 mo) median num_selected_g_fov ~= 40; scaled to 66 mo, median ~= 60-70 usable G FOV transits. Mean spacing 2010/65 ~= 31 d, but clustered: FOV pairs 106.5 min apart, groups within ~1 d, then gaps of weeks-months set by the 63-d precession.

DETECTION EFFICIENCY vs dip duration T, P(>=1 transit in dip) = 1 - exp(-N*T/T_span), N=65:
 T=1 d -> 3.2% | T=10 d -> 28% | T=30 d -> 62% | T=100 d -> 96% | T=1 yr -> ~100%.
So the lane only works for T >~ 20 d. Real big dippers last weeks-months, so this is fine — but it means the lane is a LONG-EVENT lane, and long events are exactly what GSA is best at catching (many scans inside the event, both FOVs, repeated significance). The lane's efficiency curve and GSA's efficiency curve peak in the same place. That is the single worst structural fact here.

THE "2 FOV TRANSITS" GATE IS WEAKER THAN CLAIMED. Gaia transits come in FOV pairs 106.5 min apart. For any T > ~4 hr, catching one transit almost always catches its partner — so "require >=2 FOV transits inside the dip" is nearly free and provides NO independent epoch. It kills single-CCD glitches. It does NOT kill a 2-hour instrumental excursion (attitude excursion, background failure near a bright source, diffraction spike), which is the dominant artifact class. The lane presents this as its rule-10 analogue; it is not. Rule 10 required same-night reproduction in a genuinely independent frame. This gate is one 106-minute window.

YIELD. Rate from JoHantgen+2025: 16 objects / (5.1e6 stars * ~10 yr) = 3.1e-7 per star-year (ASAS-SN efficiency ~1 for T>days). Lane assumed 5e-7 — optimistic by 1.6x, and the sign of the bias is wrong in a second way: ASAS-SN's g<14 sample is giant-rich, and deep long dips need a big star for a disk to occult for months. A G 17-19 Gaia sample is dwarf-dominated, so the intrinsic rate should be LOWER, not equal.
 Usable Gaia sample after num_selected_g_fov>=30 and 14<G<19: call it 2.0e8 of the 4.03e8 vari_summary rows.
 Events occurring: 2.0e8 * 3.1e-7 * 5.5 yr = 341.
 x duration-averaged efficiency ~0.5 -> ~170 detectable all-sky. Lane claimed 300-500. Lane is 2-3x optimistic before the giant-fraction correction.
 Minus GSA's ~46% already alerted, minus the OGLE/VVV footprint -> ~50-90 all-sky residual, of which the genuinely-new southern-faint slice is ~30-60. Nonzero. Not 100-200.

PURITY — THIS IS WHERE IT BREAKS. Gaia DR3 docs: ~30 per million sources show anomalous flux behaviour, spurious classes named literally "big dippers" and attitude excursions. Over 4.03e8 rows that is ~12,000 spurious sources against ~170 real. Raw ratio 1:70. Independently, Hodgkin+2021 report that ENVIRONMENT-aware filtering (crowding, bright neighbours, diffraction spikes) cuts candidate alerts by a further factor of ~50 — that is the filter doing the real work, and it needs image/environment information a TAP-only approach does not have.
 The lane's own Stage 1 predicts 1e5-3e5 survivors. Getting from 3e5 to ~170 needs a rejection factor of ~2000. The lane budgets "willingness to hand-vet a few hundred candidates." At 5 s per light curve, 2e5 candidates is ~280 hours of eyeballing. The labor estimate is off by 2-3 orders of magnitude, and the decisive vetting lever (environment) is precisely what the TAP-only design gives up.

COVERAGE CLAIM IS OVERSTATED BY ~4 MAGNITUDES. ATLAS-south first light 2021-22 (TRUE, ATLAS-Hawaii reaches only dec >~ -45). But ASAS-SN Chile has run since 2013 in V to V~17, and all-sky g to g~18.5 since 2017. So 14<G<17 at dec<-30 WAS covered from 2014, and 14<G<18.5 from 2017. The genuinely uncovered slice is G~18-19, i.e. ~1 mag, not the 5 mag the headline implies. Subtract OGLE-IV (~3,000 deg^2 southern disk + bulge, I<21, hours-days cadence, 2010-2020) and VVV/VVVX (~560 deg^2), which eat the densest part of it. Unique window = a ~1 mag slice over maybe 30-50% of the southern sky.

CENSORING CHANNEL (missing-transit / GOST comparison) IS THE BEST IDEA IN THE LANE and is under-developed. A >2.7 mag dip on G~18 falls below the G~20.7 onboard limit and appears as ABSENT transits — this is the project's verified lever #1 applied to Gaia, it is genuinely orthogonal to GSA (GSA needs detections; this channel is defined by their absence), and GOST gives predicted visit times for free. It is also the only part of the lane that is not a skewness cut everyone else will run on 2 Dec. If this lane proceeds, this should be the PRIMARY channel, not a footnote.
access_ok:
CONDITIONAL — and this is the unaddressed hard blocker for THIS person specifically.

Gaia TAP at gea.esac.esa.int allows anonymous queries, but anonymous sessions are capped (synchronous results ~2,000 rows; async job quotas, result-set retention, and — critically — USER TABLE UPLOAD for crossmatch are reserved for registered accounts; registered users get ~3e6-row async results). The lane's Stage 1 returns 1e5-3e5 rows and Stage 3 requires crossmatching those against external catalogues. Both realistically need a logged-in Gaia Archive account. THE PERSON CANNOT REGISTER NEW ACCOUNTS. The lane never mentions this once, despite being named "TAP-only". This is the most likely way the lane dies on a Tuesday in December.

Mitigations exist but are unverified: the Gaia@AIP mirror (gaia.aip.de) exposes gaiadr3/gaiadr4 TAP and may have different anonymous limits; VizieR/CDS TAP will mirror at least the summary tables; ESAC publishes bulk datalink/epoch-photometry products over plain HTTP that can be pulled without TAP at all. None of these is established for DR4-day-1 vari_summary access.

DataLink epoch_photometry in 5,000-ID chunks: 2e5 IDs = 40 chunk calls, trivially fine on bandwidth, but DataLink is throttled per session and the lane itself concedes week-1 archive congestion. Note the project's own verified lever #4: an archive that rate-limits by returning EMPTY 200s manufactures nulls silently. A DR4-week-1 congested archive is the highest-risk environment this project has ever queried, and the lane has no integrity check against truncated/empty returns.

Compute (6-core box) and storage are fine — the whole point of the TAP pre-filter is avoiding the 7.2 TB epoch_photometry bulk, and that part of the design is sound. 400 TB total DR4 volume is never touched.

Timing: DR4 is public 2 Dec 2026, confirmed on the ESA content page and by ESA/Gaia social accounts. Nothing here is behind a proprietary period. DR3 (for the dry run) is fully public NOW.
cheapest_kill_test:
Run the EXACT Stage-1 vari_summary query against gaiadr3, anonymously, from the 6-core box, THIS WEEK. One afternoon answers three separate kill questions at once:

(1) ACCESS GO/NO-GO. Does anonymous TAP return >2,000 rows, and can DataLink epoch_photometry be pulled without a login? If no, the lane is dead for a person who cannot register accounts, and that is settled in 20 minutes rather than on 2 Dec in a congested archive. Add an explicit integrity assert (row count > 0 AND a known-present control ID appears) so a throttled empty-200 cannot masquerade as a null — lever #4.

(2) TEMPLATE RECOVERY, per rule 7. Does the query, ON ITS OWN CONFIGURATION, recover TYC 2505-672-1, EE Cep-class objects, and those of the 16 ASAS-SN big dippers (arXiv:2507.19594) that have DR3 epoch photometry? If it recovers 0 controls while returning 1e4 survivors, the cuts are wrong and DR4 will multiply the mess by 40x. This is non-negotiable before any December effort.

(3) THE PRIOR-ART KILL. Take the clean survivors and cone-match them against the Gaia Alerts index (gsaweb.ast.cam.ac.uk, fully public, every Gaia14xxx-Gaia26xxx) plus SIMBAD and VSX. If >90% of the vetted DR3 single-dip survivors are already named Gaia alerts, then GSA has already harvested this channel down to Gaia's own photometric floor and the DR4 residual is noise, not discovery — lane closed for the cost of one day. If a meaningful fraction are GSA-silent, that number IS the lane's yield multiplier and it is measured rather than assumed.

Bonus, and the reason to do this regardless: the DR3 run is itself a live discovery run on public data available today, not just preparation. If it surfaces even one GSA-silent, VSX-absent deep dip, that is a filable object in September 2026 instead of a bet on December.

Second, cheaper-still test if (1)-(3) pass: pick 200 DR3 sources with GOST-predicted visits and compare predicted-vs-actual transit counts, to see whether the censoring channel (lever #1 applied to Gaia's onboard G~20.7 limit) is separable from ordinary scanning-law gaps. That channel is the only genuinely un-scooped part of this lane; validate it before betting on the skewness cut that everyone else will also run.
biggest_risk:
The lane's efficiency curve and Gaia Photometric Science Alerts' efficiency curve peak on the SAME events. Both need long-duration dips with many in-event scans; GSA has been catching exactly those, on exactly these photons, all-sky including the plane and bulge, in real time since 2014, publishing each one with a name at the moment of detection. The lane never mentions GSA. So the most likely outcome is not a null — it is a few hundred hours of vetting that produces a candidate list whose every clean member already has a Gaia17xxx designation, discovered years ago by the same spacecraft.

The second risk compounds it: the arithmetic is 1:70 signal-to-artifact before vetting (~12,000 Gaia-documented spurious "big dippers"/attitude excursions across 403M rows vs ~170 real events), the filter that actually works is environment-based (Hodgkin+2021: a further factor ~50), and the TAP-only design deliberately gives up the environment information. The "require 2 FOV transits" gate does not compensate — those two transits are 106 minutes apart and are not independent epochs.

Third, and most likely to end it before any of that matters: Stage 1 returns 1e5-3e5 rows and Stage 3 needs table-upload crossmatch, both of which want a registered Gaia Archive account. This person cannot register accounts. A lane whose name is "TAP-only" has not checked whether anonymous TAP can do what it asks.

prior_art_found:
No prior art found, after 8 searches, for the specific selection axis: joining ZTF DR light curves to ztf_current_meta_ref reference windows and selecting on in-window vs out-window brightness. The axis appears genuinely unclaimed. What DOES threaten the lane is adjacent, and it threatens the OBJECTS rather than the METHOD:

(1) SNAD Transient Miner (arXiv:2111.11555, Astron.Comput. 2022) mined ZTF DR4 for transients missed by the alert stream: 11 transients, 3 absent from the alert stream. (2) "Supernova search with active learning in ZTF DR3" (A&A 2023, aa45172-22): 15 possible SNe missing from the official ZTF alert stream. (3) SNAD anomaly detection DR3 (MNRAS 502, 5147) and DR23 (arXiv:2507.06217) — the latter got 6 uncatalogued variables from 4 fields, consistent with the ~1.5/field kill threshold already banked in this project. (4) DR-based bulk variable catalogues that would already contain these objects as high-amplitude variable candidates even if unlabelled: Ofek/ZTF DR1 10M variable candidates (MNRAS 499, 5782), Chen+2020 781k periodics, Healy+2024 ZTF SCP, and "Persistent and occasional" ZTF DR11 (arXiv:2304.08519), which explicitly targets non-periodic "occasional" variables. (5) Reference contamination itself is documented, not secret: Dhawan+2022 / ZTF SN Ia DR2 (A&A 2025, aa48476-23) describe transient flux in references producing negative alerts, and the ZTF forced-photometry service returns refjdstart/refjdend per position, so the per-object information is public and routinely used — only the population-scale join is missing.

Alert-based CV work (Szkody+2021 ZTF year-2 CVs; Duffy+2024 ML CV discovery, MNRAS 527, 8633) is structurally blind to this population, so the lane's core argument survives on that flank.

scooped_fraction_estimate: Method axis: ~0% scooped. Objects: strongly tier-dependent. Tier 2 (long windows: Z Cam standstills, nova-likes, symbiotics, AGN flares) ~70-85% scooped — a source bright enough to dominate a multi-year, 15-40 frame outlier-rejected co-add is by construction bright and persistent, and is almost certainly already in VSX/SIMBAD/Chen+2020. Tier 1 (short windows, dwarf novae / AM CVn / EXor) ~30-50% scooped against VSX. The 2018-SNe sub-claim ~60-80% scooped by SNAD DR3/DR4 transient mining plus contemporaneous ATLAS/ASAS-SN/Gaia Alerts coverage above r~19.5. Net realistic novel yield: order 10-40 VSX-submittable uncatalogued outbursting systems, NOT the claimed 100-300.
why_not_done_claim_credible:
Partly credible, partly self-serving — and I can separate the two with measurements.

CREDIBLE: (a) brokers and alert-based CV searches genuinely cannot see these objects (Szkody+2021, Duffy+2024 both work from alerts); (b) the DR parquet genuinely does not carry the reference window, so no DR-based catalogue has used it as a selection axis — I confirmed the DR-side absence and confirmed the metadata lives only in a separate IRSA table; (c) Dhawan+2022 genuinely fixed reference contamination only for its own SN sample; (d) the join really does cost one TAP query — I ran it in 48 s.

SELF-SERVING: (a) "DR-based catalogues never use the reference window" is true but slides into an implied "so these objects are uncatalogued", which does not follow — a source with a >=1 mag excursion is a high-amplitude DR variable and will already sit in the 10M-candidate DR1 list and plausibly in the DR11 "occasional" search; the axis is new, the objects largely are not; (b) it omits that SNAD already mined DR for alert-missed transients twice and measured yields of ~10-15, which is the honest prior for this population; (c) the phrase "generalises the J075308 lesson to a population" borrows credibility from a single verified object without showing the population exists. The lane is right that nobody has turned this screw. It is wrong to imply nobody has been in the room.
depth_arithmetic:
I did not accept the lane's window-length premise — I downloaded the table and measured it. IRSA TAP sync, ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref, 9 columns, 196,357 rows in 48 s, no auth. (Lane said 177,984 rows; stale but right order. Columns are exactly as claimed: field, ccdid, qid, rcid, filtercode, nframes, maglimit, startobsdate, endobsdate.)

MEASURED reference-window span distribution, all 196,357 rows, zero parse failures:
p5 = 30.0 d | p10 = 39.9 d | p25 = 93.9 d | MEDIAN = 282.1 d | p75 = 606.4 d | p90 = 1392.2 d.
<=30 d: 9,683 (4.93%). <=60 d: 29,142 (14.84%). <=90 d: 46,539 (23.70%). <=365 d: 109,500 (55.77%).
By filter: zr 79,412 refs, median 251 d, only 3,199 (4.03%) <=30 d; zg 75,761, median 273 d, 3,456 (4.56%); zi 41,184, median 400 d, 3,028 (7.35%).
nframes: median 15, p10 15, p90 33. Short-window refs (<=30 d) have median nframes 15 — i.e. 15 frames inside 30 days.

THIS KILLS TIER 1 OUTSIDE ~5% OF SKY. ZTF references are outlier-rejected co-adds of >=15 frames. To poison a reference at the >=1.0 mag level the lane's own criterion (2) demands, the source must be bright in a MAJORITY of co-added frames. In the median 282-day window with 15-33 frames, a 10-20 d dwarf-nova superoutburst contributes 1-3 frames and is rejected by the clipping: the reference is clean, the source alerts normally, and there is nothing to find. Tier 1 therefore lives only in the 4.93% short-window subset.

SKY AREA: zr short-window sky = 3,199 quadrants x ~0.73 deg^2 per ZTF CCD-quadrant ~= 2,340 deg^2, i.e. ~7.8% of the ~30,000 deg^2 public footprint.

TIER 1 YIELD, honestly: VSX holds ~15,300 CVs all-sky; ZTF-detectable outbursting CVs known+unknown call it 15,000-20,000. In 7.8% of sky: ~1,200-1,600. Each needs an outburst covering >=half of a 30-day/15-frame window — a superoutburst (10-20 d) at the right phase; DN outburst duty cycle ~5-10% and the phase must align, so a few percent at best. => order 20-60 poisoned systems total, majority already catalogued (they are catalogued precisely because they are the bright active ones). Novel Tier 1: ~5-25 objects. The lane's headline 100-300 is ~10x optimistic.

TIER 2 is where the N is (55.77% of refs have windows >365 d) and it is exactly the tier where novelty is worst — see scooped_fraction_estimate. The lane's N and its novelty are anti-correlated and the lane never says so.

2018-SNe SUB-CLAIM IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN PIPELINE: criterion (2) requires >=20 catflags-clean detections OUTSIDE the reference window. A 2018 SN at 19.5<r<20.5 has essentially zero out-window detections — it faded below the DR floor (project lever 1: no rows). The stated selection cannot deliver those objects at all; a different pipeline is required, and that pipeline is SNAD Transient Miner's territory with a measured yield of ~10.

CONFIRMATION GAP: DR24 parquet lacks refmag (the lane admits this). "In-window bright in DR" does not prove the reference is poisoned — you cannot know what fraction of co-added frames caught the outburst. So the advertised refereeable byproduct ("how many ZTF references are poisoned") is NOT measurable by this pipeline as specified. refmag is obtainable from the ZTF forced-photometry service, but that is email-gated and returns browser downloads (already banked in this project), so it is a real bottleneck at the 5,000-object stage, not a one-liner.
access_ok: Yes, verified live today, no new accounts needed. (1) IRSA TAP sync https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/TAP/sync, table ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref: full 196,357-row pull, 9 columns, 48 s, anonymous, single query — I executed it. (2) ZTF DR24 is public: released 2026-01-22, covering 2018-03 through 2025-10-22 (DR25 scheduled 2027-01-20), so the archive is live and ~11 months stale by project-run time. Light curves on public S3 HATS/parquet, no account. (3) CRITICAL COST CONTROL the lane misses: do NOT scan all of DR24 (~3-4 TB; days of I/O on a 6-core box). Pull only the HATS partitions matching the 3,199 zr + 3,456 zg short-window quadrants — ~5% of the archive, ~1 night on enzo. (4) ALeRCE public API for per-object alert lists, batched at the ~5,000-object stage only, with explicit empty-200 checks. (5) IRSA per-position API must NOT be used for bulk — the ~1,100-query ceiling returning empty 200s is already a banked failure mode of this project and would manufacture a false null. (6) ZTF forced photometry (for refmag confirmation) is email-gated and browser-download-based: the real friction point.
cheapest_kill_test:
Run the template test BEFORE any search, on the restricted short-window set, and make it a known-object recovery test rather than the lane's SN-only control. Concretely, in ~1-2 days: take the 3,199 zr quadrants with windows <=30 d; cross-match VSX dwarf novae and AM CVn systems falling in those quadrants; for each, check whether a known outburst epoch lands inside its own quadrant's reference window; pull only those HATS partitions and run criterion (2) unchanged. Then measure two numbers: (a) what fraction of known DNe with a superoutburst inside their own <=30 d reference window are recovered by the >=1.0 mag in-vs-out-window median cut, and (b) for those recovered, does ALeRCE show zero positive alerts over 2018-2025?

If (a) is near zero, the 15-frame outlier-rejected co-add is simply not poisoned by a 10-20 d superoutburst, Tier 1 dies outright, and Tier 2 alone — the high-N, low-novelty tier — is not worth three weeks. If (a) is healthy but (b) fails (the objects alerted anyway), the causal premise is wrong and the lane dies regardless of yield. Either way it is decided in days on free data, with no new accounts and no telescope. Add the Dhawan+2022 reference-contaminated SNe Ia as a second control only after this one passes; it tests a different tier and cannot rescue Tier 1.
biggest_risk: The lane's N and its novelty are anti-correlated, and the lane does not admit it. The 4.93% of references with short windows are the only place a dwarf-nova-class outburst can actually dominate an outlier-rejected 15-frame co-add — that tier has genuine novelty but yields order 5-25 objects. The 55.77% with year-plus windows yield plenty of flags, but anything bright enough to poison a multi-year co-add is a persistent bright variable already in VSX/SIMBAD. So the expected outcome is not a clean null; it is a few thousand flags that vet down to a couple of dozen genuinely new objects after weeks of labour, with the project's own ~1.5-uncatalogued-per-field SNAD threshold sitting right at the edge of that. Secondary risk: without refmag the poisoning itself is never confirmed, so every candidate carries an unproven causal claim and the advertised population-level byproduct cannot be delivered. Tertiary: the 2018-SNe half needs TNS filing, which the account constraint blocks, and needs a pipeline the lane did not specify.
one_line_reason: The selection axis is genuinely unclaimed after 8 searches, the data is public and I pulled it today in 48 s, and the comparison is intra-ZTF-DR — same pipeline, same source — so it escapes the blend/sub-threshold artefact trap that definitionally satisfied the closed turn-on lane; but my own measurement of the window distribution (median 282 d, only 4.93% <=30 d, median 15 frames) cuts the claimed 100-300 yield by roughly 10x, strands the high-N tier in the low-novelty regime, and exposes that the 2018-SNe sub-claim cannot be produced by the lane's own selection criteria — so it earns a cheap gated pilot, not a three-week commitment.

scooped_fraction_estimate: ~20% of the Stage-1 footprint is pre-chewed: COSMOS and ELAIS-S1 (2 of 10 DES-SN fields) already have public Graham DDF DIA light curves, and COSMOS additionally has HSC-SSP transient coverage. The specific product — a faint (r_q > 21) DN/period-bouncer outburst census from DECam per-exposure data, filed to VSX/TNS — is 0% scooped as far as 13 searches can show. But the headline population claim (500-750 CVs in the DES-wide footprint, 200-400 with a caught outburst) is ~50-70% pre-empted in practice by CRTS (2005-2013, V<19-20, dec>-75), ASAS-SN (2014+, g<18) and ATLAS-south (2022+, o<19.5), which will already have registered any CV whose outbursts peak brighter than ~19.5. The truly-new residue is only the sub-19.5-peak tail.
why_not_done_claim_credible: Mostly credible, with one self-serving passage. Credible: I verified from the release paper that DES-SN's own product is SN-selected (SMP is "not guaranteed to converge for candidates with multi-season variability"; the multi-season cut exists explicitly "to remove AGNs and long-lived transients"), that DES's published wide variable-star work is RR Lyrae only, that HELM is an AGN-RM programme, and that the DECam DDF papers classify stellar variables generically without a CV sample. The "everyone who held these photons treated dwarf novae as contamination" claim survives contact with the literature. The 2013-2019 southern epochs genuinely cannot be scooped by Rubin, and ATLAS-south/BlackGEM only start 2022+. Self-serving: the lane says NSC's MAD variability indices barely move for a single 2-mag epoch (true) and presents that as the reason nobody has mined NSC meas — but the real reason nobody works at quiescent r = 23.5-24.5 in NSC is that NSC per-exposure DECam data does not reach there at all, which the lane never concedes. It also frames the lane as a period-bouncer search while every classification step that would actually establish a period bouncer (spectrum, orbital period, donor mass) is telescope-gated and out of reach.
depth_arithmetic: SPACE DENSITY, recomputed independently. Pala+2020 n0 = 4.8e-6 pc^-3, exponential scale height 280 pc, column N = n0 * dOmega * 2h^3 / sin^3|b|. DES-SN fields sit at |b| ~ 45-65: N = 0.086 (b=65), 0.099 (b=60), 0.121 (b=54), 0.182 (b=45) CV/deg^2, FULL column to infinity, all magnitudes. STAGE 1 IS THEREFORE OVER-CLAIMED: 27 deg^2 x ~0.12 = 3.2 CVs total in the whole DES-SN footprint, not the "5-16" the lane states from an assumed 0.2-0.6 deg^-2 (that figure is 2-5x too high for |b| = 45-65; it is a |b| ~ 30 number). With ~70% having r_q > 21 and some already in VSX/CRTS, the honest Stage-1 expectation is 0-3 new faint CVs, most likely 1. Detection efficiency on that small parent sample is high, which is the redeeming part: ~7-day griz cadence, ~20 epochs/season/filter, 5 seasons, shallow fields r ~ 23.5 and deep fields r ~ 24.5 single-epoch, and DiffImg light curves are FORCED at the mean candidate position across all epochs — so a 2-5 mag outburst lasting 1-4 weeks is caught and its duration measured, which separates DN outbursts from flares. Stage 3 density checks out: 5,000 deg^2 at |b| ~ 45 gives ~900 CVs full-column, consistent with the lane's 500-750 to r=23.5. STAGE 3 DEPTH FAILS ON ITS OWN TERMS. DES wide single exposures are 90 s, 10-sigma r ~ 23.0-23.3, and NSC DR2 median depth10sig in r is ~22.5. A source at quiescent r = 23.5-24.5 produces ZERO meas rows in every exposure, so it cannot be an nsc_dr2.object with ndet >= 6. The pre-cut "median r 21.5-24.5 AND ndet >= 6" is only physically populated over roughly 21.5-23.2, and at its faint end the object median is detection-biased bright, which is exactly the regime where the closed turn-on lane died. Consequently the "10-20 hostless period-bouncer candidates (quiescent M_r ~ 12-13, r > 24.5)" can ONLY come from the branch with no static counterpart — i.e. the lane's most valuable claimed yield rests entirely on its least verifiable channel. VOLUME: point-source counts at r 21.5-23 at |b|>30 are ~1,000-2,000 deg^-2 (lane's own 2,008 deg^-2 at r 20-22.5), so Stage 3's pre-cut set is ~5-10 million objects x ~30-50 meas epochs = 1.5-5 x 10^8 meas rows to pull. HELM/recurrence check is sound: HELM DR1 covers COSMOS, XMM-LSS, CDF-S, ELAIS-S1, S-CVZ, Stripe 82 at few-day cadence 2019-2022, directly overlapping the DES-SN deep fields, giving an independent 3-year recurrence window after the DES seasons end.
access_ok: Stage 1: YES, unambiguously. DES-SN5YR is a downloadable file set (github.com/des-science/DES-SN5YR, Zenodo 12720778), 31,636 DiffImg light curves, griz, no account, no rate limit, fits on the 6-core box. HELM DR1 light curves are served from an open HTTP directory. DES DR2 coadds and the Y3 deep-field catalogue are public via NOIRLab/Data Lab. LS DR10 sweeps are bulk-downloadable. This stage touches no rate-limited per-position API. Stage 3: MARGINAL-TO-NO. The user cannot register accounts, so no Data Lab MyDB and no server-side crossmatch of an uploaded target list. Anonymous Data Lab TAP is the only route; it already rejects q3c and ADQL POINT/CIRCLE (the project has measured this), sync queries are row- and time-capped, and joining against the 67.8e9-row nsc_dr2.meas without MyDB means ra/dec-box-driven pulls of order 1.5-5 x 10^8 rows. That is not a 1-2 week job, and it runs straight into verified lever #4: the service returns empty 200s rather than errors when it throttles, so a throttled run manufactures a null. If Stage 3 is attempted it needs a measured rows-per-hour and empty-response rate on a single field BEFORE any footprint-scale pull, and an explicit non-empty-response assert on every batch. SkyMapper DR4 anonymous TAP (r ~ 21) and ZTF ZFPS (dec > -31 sliver, bound to the user's existing TU Delft-linked account) are fine as bright-end controls.
cheapest_kill_test: One day, one downloaded file, zero API risk: pull the DES-SN5YR DiffImg release and run the template-recovery gate required by lever #7 BEFORE any search. Take every VSX/CRTS/ASAS-SN known dwarf nova and known CV whose position falls inside the 27 deg^2 of the ten DES-SN fields, and ask two questions. (a) Do they appear in the 31,636 released DiffImg candidates at all, with a recognisable outburst light curve? If known DNe inside the footprint are largely ABSENT from the released list, then the DES real-time candidate stream or the release packaging silently removed Galactic outbursters and the lane has no supply — dead at zero cost, and no NSC pull is ever attempted. (b) Independently of the known objects, count how many candidates in the 31,636 are coincident within 1" with a static point source in the DES deep coadds AND show one or more isolated 1-4 week brightenings rather than an SN-like single rise-and-decay. If that count is ~0-3 and all of them are already in VSX, the recomputed 3.2-CV column density is confirmed, Stage 1 yields nothing new, and Stage 3's 100x labor for a 30x larger area at shallower depth is not worth starting. This single test measures the parent population, validates the pipeline on its own templates, and sets the stop rule, all before a byte of NSC meas is requested.
biggest_risk: M-dwarf flares eat the Stage-3 candidate list. At |b| > 30 the r = 21-24 population is dominated by M dwarfs, flares are blue and 1-5 mag, and DES takes griz of a hex within ~10 minutes — so a single flare lasting tens of minutes produces exactly the signature Stage 3 selects: >= 2 same-night measurements, each >= 2 mag above the object median, PSF-shaped, same centroid, flags=0. The only offered veto is quiescent r-z > 1.2, which fails precisely in the faint regime where the quiescent counterpart is poorly measured or undetected, i.e. in the hostless branch that carries all the claimed period-bouncer yield. The DECam DDF papers found stellar flares as a major class in exactly these fields. NSC meas gives no intra-night duration leverage beyond the ~10-minute griz span, so Stage 3 structurally cannot separate a 30-minute flare from a 10-day outburst. Stage 1 does not have this problem — DiffImg forced light curves resolve outburst duration — which is the real reason the lane's value is concentrated in its cheapest stage. Secondary risk: the hostless branch's "no counterpart to r ~ 24.5-26.5 in a deeper dataset" is the same deep-sharp-versus-shallow-coarse absence claim that killed the turn-on lane, re-imported with the roles reversed; the same-instrument fix protects the detection side but not this veto side.
one_line_reason: Stage 1 only: the DES-SN5YR DiffImg release is a free download with forced multi-epoch photometry over 27 deg^2 of 2013-2018 southern sky that nobody has mined for Galactic accretors, VSX/TNS will register what it finds, and one day of template recovery kills it if the supply is not there — but the lane's headline numbers are inflated 2-5x by a wrong CV column density (3 CVs in the DES-SN footprint, not 5-16), and Stage 3 must be refused as written because NSC DR2 per-exposure DECam photometry does not reach the quiescent r = 23.5-24.5 sources its entire period-bouncer yield is built on.

scooped_fraction_estimate: Split, because the two halves have very different exposure. (A) emission-line census: ~65-80% scooped inside the exploitation window. The HRSC (forced photometry at external-catalogue positions, SNR>10 in >=5 channels) is functionally the same engine, all-sky, mission-built, landing ~mid-2027; once it drops, computing a line index E from it is a one-day exercise for anyone, and the Pa/Br emission-line point-source case is a pre-advertised mission deliverable (arXiv:1606.07039) held by a team already publishing plane Br-alpha work. Realistic usable window: ~9 months from today, minus 2-4 months of engine build = ~5 months of exploitation. (B) new-source sweep: ~15-30% scooped. The incumbent group disclaims the pipeline in print, so the archival-discovery niche is genuinely open; the leakage is that PRIME (southern, bulge, alerts), PGIR, and optical surveys will independently find a fraction of the same events first, and any single event has a real chance of being reported by someone else before a weekly sweep reaches it (this project has already lost AT 2026uxw by 25 hours).
why_not_done_claim_credible:
Mostly credible on (B), self-serving on (A), plus two factual errors.

CREDIBLE AND UNUSUALLY WELL-EVIDENCED: the (B) claim. I went looking for the incumbents' stated plans expecting the usual "they are obviously about to do this," and instead found them stating the opposite in their own words: SPHEREx classifies, other surveys discover. That is the strongest form this argument can take. The LVF + 3-6" PSF genuinely does make classical difference imaging awkward, IRSA genuinely ships no bulk extraction, and the "what changed vs the dead IR-nova lane" answer (new mission, new 2025-26 epoch, NEOWISE dead since Aug 2024) is a real change rather than a reframing.

SELF-SERVING: the (A) claim. "Emission-line specialists are optical/spectroscopic and small" and "Crowther's group just spent its effort on Gaia XP WR candidates" are arguments about who is busy, not about whether the niche is open. The niche is not open: it is a published, pre-registered mission science case, and the mission is about to hand the community the catalogue that makes the engine unnecessary. Framing a 9-month race against a funded team's scheduled data product as a "window" is exactly the self-serving move this gate exists to catch. The lane also quietly omits that HRSC is built by forced photometry at external-catalogue positions -- i.e. the mission is doing lane (A)'s engine, at higher fidelity, with the instrument team's PSF and flux calibration.

FACTUALLY WRONG, both in the lane's favour: (i) "most south of dec -20 where no IR time-domain survey operates (WINTER/PGIR north; VVVX ended 2023; Gattini ended)" -- PRIME is southern, live, bulge-focused, alert-issuing, and is named as ongoing in the very paper the lane cites; PGIR is called "ongoing" by the incumbents too. (ii) The lane's citation of arXiv:2607.02809 as "about particle hits" is correct (it is South Atlantic Anomaly transient-flagging rates), so that one checks out.

MERGE IS FAKE: the lane is sold as "one forced-PSF-photometry engine ... feeds two products." It is not. (A) is forced photometry at ~1e7 known positions across 102 channels; (B) is blind detection plus catalogue-based rejection in 3 bands. They share an S3 bucket and a PSF model, nothing else. The merge manufactures an efficiency that does not exist and hides the fact that (A) carries ~85% of the labor.
depth_arithmetic:
I verified the lane's own numbers and recomputed the ones it did not show.

CHANNEL WIDTHS AND EW THRESHOLDS (E = EW/delta-lambda):
- Pa-alpha 1.875 um, band 3, R=41 -> 457 A. E>=0.15 -> EW>=69 A. Lane's "~457 A / ~70 A" is CORRECT.
- Br-alpha 4.05 um is in band 5 (3.82-4.42 um), R~112, NOT R~130 (that is band 6). Width 362 A, so E>=0.15 -> EW>=54 A, not the claimed 47 A. 17% optimistic.
- Br-gamma 2.166 um, band 3, R=41 -> 528 A -> E>=0.15 needs EW>=79 A. Symbiotic Br-gamma EW reaches ~41 A at most (literature), giving E~0.078. THE "He I 1.083 + Br-gamma" CONFIRMATION PAIR CANNOT FIRE FOR SYMBIOTICS. Only Pa-alpha+Br-alpha works there (symbiotic Br-alpha EW up to ~740 A -> E~2.0, comfortable).

WHERE THE YIELD ESTIMATE BREAKS: classical Be stars have H-alpha EW ~5-40 A and near-IR hydrogen EWs comparable or weaker -- Pa-alpha EW of order tens of A -> E ~ 0.02-0.09, BELOW the 0.15 floor. Tier B ("~2,000-5,000, about half uncatalogued") therefore collapses to the extreme B[e]/strong-emitter tail; realistic 200-800, i.e. overstated 5-10x. Tier A survives cleanly: WR near-IR He/H lines EW 50-500 A -> E 0.11-1.1; PNe and strong symbiotics far above threshold. So the honest product of (A) is ~100-400 WR/symbiotic/PN-like candidates, not a Be census.

CONTINUUM SNR: 4-pass 5sigma is 19.3-19.7 AB at 0.75-3.8 um; one pass is ~0.75 mag shallower = 18.55-18.95 AB. SNR>=20 is 4x above 5sigma = 1.5 mag brighter = 17.05 AB. Target K=14.0 Vega = 15.85 AB. Margin 1.2 mag -- the K<=14 cut is correctly placed, but only barely; it fails past K~15.2, and the published curves explicitly EXCLUDE source confusion.

CONFUSION -- the unacknowledged problem for (A): beam ~pi(3.1")^2 = 30 arcsec^2 = 2.3e-6 deg^2. At the standard 1 source per 30 beams the confusion limit is ~1.4e4 sources/deg^2. VVV counts at K<14 in the inner plane (|l|<30, |b|<1) are ~2-5e4/deg^2. SPHEREx is ABOVE its own confusion limit across the inner plane. The 12" isolation cut passes ~71% at 1e4/deg^2, ~50% at 2e4, and only ~17% at 5e4 -- so the inner plane, which is where the missing obscured WR/symbiotic population actually lives, is where the sample is thinnest. Worse, residual sub-threshold blends dilute the line index: a 30% continuum blend drops E by 23%, pushing the already-marginal Tier B further under.

(B) DEPTH -- arithmetic is correct but the yield is not: single-pass 5sigma at 3.8-5.0 um = 17.05-18.05 AB, matching the lane exactly. W1-eq 15.0 Vega = 17.70 AB, W2-eq 13.5 Vega = 16.84 AB, both above the limit. But note what that means: SPHEREx band 5-6 single-pass reaches W2 ~13.5 Vega while NEOWISE single exposures reached W2 ~15 Vega. SPHEREx is ~1.5 mag SHALLOWER at 4.6 um than the dead archive it replaces. The lever is purely temporal, which is legitimate but narrow, and the lane never says so.

NOVA YIELD: NEOWISE empirically recovered ~22 missed novae in 10 yr = 2.2/yr, essentially all in the plane. Lane area ~1,100 deg^2 is ~55% of the missed-nova sky. Window 16 months = 1.33 yr. SPHEREx completes a position's spectrum in a ~2-week window per ~6-month pass, so the temporal duty cycle against a 2-4 month IR-bright nova is ~55%. Product: 2.2 x 1.33 x 0.55 x 0.55 = 0.9 novae. The lane claims 3-6. Overstated 3-7x. Add eruptive YSOs/FUors (all-sky detected rate ~1-2/yr, so <1 in this area) and the honest expectation for (B) is 1-3 genuinely new objects, not 13-36.

VOLUME/COMPUTE: (A) 1.4 TB streamed over two passes; 1e7 targets x 102 channels = 1e9 forced measurements, ~1.9 days of pure 6-core CPU at 1 ms each, realistically 1-2 weeks with I/O -- the compute is fine, the pipeline development is not.

cheapest_kill_test:
A two-day control-recovery run that tests the engine and the line-index threshold at the same time, before any survey code is written.

Pull SPHEREx QR2 MEFs for ~60 positions: (i) ~40 CATALOGUED emission-line stars spanning the claimed tiers at K=10-14 in the plane -- Rosslowe & Crowther WR, NODSV symbiotics, HASH PNe, and critically ~15 BeSS classical Be stars; (ii) the 3 novae and 2 FUors of Karambelkar+2026 (arXiv:2602.07129), which have PUBLISHED SPHEREx spectra; (iii) ~15 ordinary M giants as the H2O-trough false-positive control. Do the forced PSF extraction, compute E = (F_line - F_cont)/F_cont at Pa-alpha, Pa-beta, Br-alpha, Br-gamma, He I 1.083, and answer two questions:

1. ENGINE (project lever 7): does your extraction reproduce the five published Karambelkar spectra to within ~20%? If not, both halves are dead on day one and you have spent two days, not three months.
2. THRESHOLD: what fraction of catalogued Be stars actually reach E>=0.15 in >=2 lines? My arithmetic says most land at E ~ 0.02-0.09 and Tier B evaporates. If measured Be recovery is below ~30%, (A)'s headline yield of 2,000-5,000 is fiction and the lane reduces to a few hundred WR/symbiotic/PN candidates -- still interesting, but a completely different cost-benefit. Run the same cut on the M giants: if the 1.8-2.0 um water trough alone produces E>=0.15 at Pa-alpha in more than ~10% of them, the two-line requirement is doing less work than claimed.

This is decisive because it attacks the two load-bearing assumptions (that a solo rebuild of mission spectrophotometry is achievable, and that E>=0.15 selects the named populations) with data that already exists and costs a few GB. Do NOT let the first work be the 2,000 deg^2 target-list build.
biggest_risk:
Two risks, one per half, and they are different in kind.

(A) THE CREDIT CHANNEL IS BROKEN BY THE LANE'S OWN SELECTION FUNCTION. The whole premise is objects behind A_V = 8-25. VSX requires demonstrated VARIABILITY, not an emission line, so the lane leans on "Gaia DR4 epoch photometry supplies it at scale." Run the extinction: a K=14 star behind A_V=15 has A_K~1.7, so K0~12.3; for an OB/WR-like intrinsic V-K ~ -0.8 that is V0~11.5, observed V~26.5. Invisible to Gaia. Even at the A_V=8 floor you get V~20.3, i.e. G~20 -- marginal, and only for the shallowest tail of the very population the lane exists to reach. DR4 epoch photometry cannot supply variability for most of this sample BY CONSTRUCTION. That collapses (A)'s credit path to "a catalogue paper with Crowther / Merc / Drew taking the confirming spectra" -- a relationship, not a codified mechanism, and this project's own banked lesson is "codified credit channels (MPC/VSX/TNS) > relationships." Combined with the HRSC landing mid-2027, (A) asks for ~3 months of the hardest engineering in the project's history in exchange for a candidate list that needs someone else's telescope and someone else's goodwill, inside a shrinking window, against the team that will get the catalogue first. That is the lane's true shape and it is not what the summary sells.

(B) IT SILENTLY REPLICATES THE STRUCTURE OF THE CLOSED TURN-ON LANE. The ledger records: "deep-sharp vs shallow-coarse comparison is definitionally satisfied by blends, sub-threshold noise, cosmic rays" -- 9,745 objects, 0 formal candidates. Lane (B) requires a source PRESENT in shallow-coarse SPHEREx (6.2" pixels, ~1.5 mag shallower than NEOWISE at 4.6 um) and ABSENT in deep-sharp unWISE (2.75") and VVV (0.34"), in the most crowded sky on the celestial sphere at |b|<=5. That is the same comparison, in its worst geometry, and the lane does not mention it once. The counterpart cut helps less than it looks: at inner-plane densities the 6" rejection radius contains ~0.9 sources brighter than W1=17 by chance, so it throws away roughly half of any real detections while leaving H2RG persistence latents and bright-star PSF wings in sparse patches as the surviving false-positive population. The proposed control (blind recovery of Karambelkar's 3 novae + 2 FUors) tests sensitivity but NOT the false-positive rate, which is what actually killed the predecessor lane.

Secondary: the AT 2026uxw lesson applies with full force. A weekly sweep of a survey that PRIME, PGIR and optical surveys are also watching means ~1 expected novel nova whose credit goes to whoever files first.
one_line_reason: Best-evidenced "why not done" I have gated -- the incumbents disclaim a SPHEREx discovery pipeline in print (arXiv:2602.07129) and the data is genuinely bulk-accessible with no rate limit -- but the merge is fake and the two halves fail differently: (A) is a pre-advertised mission science case racing an HRSC that lands ~mid-2027, its E>=0.15 floor overstates the Be yield 5-10x, and its A_V 8-25 targets are invisible to Gaia DR4 so its VSX channel does not exist; (B) has a clean TNS channel but ~0.9 expected novae against a claimed 3-6, rests on a false "no southern IR survey" claim that PRIME refutes, and silently rebuilds the shallow-coarse-vs-deep-sharp comparison that closed the turn-on lane at 9,745 objects and 0 candidates. Kill (A), keep (B) only as a scoped 4-6 week build, and gate it on the two-day control run before any survey code is written -- (B)-alone becomes GO_CANDIDATE if that control passes and the false-positive rate on one 50 deg^2 southern-plane patch comes in at tens rather than thousands.
