Epochs line up: Gaia DR3 photometry 2014.5-2017.4, ZTF references built 2018-2019 (gate startobsdate<2019), so the fade must begin in a ~1-4 yr window and PERSIST 8 years to 2026.

FALSE-POSITIVE ARITHMETIC -- WRONG BY ~30x. Tier 0 sets a faint cut (G<=16.5) and NO BRIGHT CUT. ZTF saturates near r~13 in 30s exposures and the reference coadds are worse; bright stars are masked, mis-centroided or absent from the reference PSF catalogue. Gaia G<13 over 25,000 deg^2 is roughly 4e6 stars. Even a 30% ZTF-absence/mismatch rate among those yields >1e6 raw non-matches against the lane's predicted 3e4 TOTAL. The stated funnel (6e7 -> 3e4 -> 1e3 -> 100-300 -> 2-10) is therefore not survivable as written. Fixable in one line (add G>13.5, costing ~7% of the sample), and the lane's own 1,000-random-star control with its >=99.9%-match stop rule would catch it in hour one -- but it shows the funnel was estimated, not computed.

ASTROPHYSICAL SUPPLY -- THIN, AND THE REAL PROBLEM. Requirement is a >=4.5 mag fade of a G<=16.5 star, onset 2014-2018, CONTINUOUS through 2026 (8+ yr). Class by class: (1) RCB in deep minimum -- ~162 known MW+MC total, maybe 50-80 at G<=16.5 in footprint; an 8-yr continuous deep minimum is the R CrB 2007-2018 record event, not typical (typical declines are months to ~2 yr), so ~2% occupancy; novel ones must have been missed by two all-sky ASAS-SN RCB campaigns plus Tisserand's WISE-based work -> expect 0-1. (2) >=8-yr giant eclipses -- Gaia17bpp's ~7 yr is the record; the total known multi-year-eclipse population is under ten objects; an eclipse spanning ALL of 2018-2026 is essentially unprecedented -> expect 0-1. (3) VY Scl deep low states -- floor is the WD/disc level, typically r~19-20 not >21, so most FAIL the Tier-0 >=4.5-mag-to-below-21 test and fall into Tier 1; and they are overwhelmingly catalogued. (4) Dust-cocooned post-AGB -- the most plausible novel class, correctly discriminated by lever 5 (LS DR10 forced unWISE, W1>19.3), but this is the same IR-variability surface the project already closed against VarWISE/Guidry. (5) Galactic N6946-BH1 analogue at G<=16.5 in a 3-yr window -- expected number ~1e-3; a lottery ticket dressed as a science case. HONEST TIER-0 YIELD: 0-2 novel, modal outcome 0-1. Not 2-10.
access_ok: YES, and this is the lane's strongest verified section -- every named endpoint is public and live right now. (1) ZTF DR24 released 2026-01-22; the ZTF DR24 HATS release went public 2026-05-26 on the AWS Registry of Open Data (anonymous S3) -- lever 4's bulk endpoint confirmed, which is what makes the ~6e7-row crossmatch feasible on 6 cores and routes around the ~1,100-query IRSA per-position rate limit that manufactures empty-200 nulls. (2) Gaia DR3 gaia_source HATS at data.lsdb.io -- public, already used by this project (135.9M-row count measured). (3) IRSA TAP ztf.ztf_current_meta_ref -- public TAP, 196,357 reference products with startobsdate/maglimit/corner coords; this is the per-quadrant coverage-proof table and it is the one thing lesson 6 absolutely requires. (4) IRSA IBE reference PSF catalogues and cutouts -- public, unauthenticated, but per-position; budget the few hundred survivor calls against the ~1,100-query wall. (5) ALeRCE and Lasair-LSST cone searches -- open; note the project's own finding that the ZTF token does not transfer to lasair.lsst.ac.uk (401) and that the Rubin alert stream has been dark since MJD 61235, so use ALeRCE as the primary ZTF-alert veto. (6) VSX / TNS / SIMBAD / Gaia Science Alerts -- open, no account. (7) THE UNUSED ONE: ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2 is open-access with a documented Python client and no registration, so the no-new-accounts constraint does not block it. ATLAS forced photometry DOES require an account and is therefore unavailable to this user -- worth noting since ATLAS (o<19.5, all-sky since 2017) would otherwise be the second independent check. Compute: a 2" LSDB crossmatch of 6e7 x ZTF DR24 objects is comfortable on 6 cores; Tier 1's ~1e8 rows is not comfortable and is where the schedule breaks.
cheapest_kill_test: Query ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2 for 1,000 random Gaia DR3 stars at 15.0 < G < 16.5 in the ZTF footprint (pyasassn, free, no account, hours not days) and measure what fraction return a real light curve with epochs spanning 2015-2026. If >~90% do -- which arXiv:2304.03791 says they will, because the 98.6M-target stellar input is ATLAS REFCAT2 at g<18.5 and is indexed by Gaia ID -- then the lane's founding premise ("invisible by construction") is dead on the spot, before a single row of the 6e7 x ZTF DR24 crossmatch is computed. The lane does not then become worthless; it becomes a DIFFERENT and much cheaper lane: skip ZTF entirely and search the ASAS-SN v2 light curves directly at 14.5 < g < 16.5 for deep permanent fades, which is one magnitude slice above where the incumbent has published (13<g<14 and 13<g<14.5) and which they will take next. Run this test FIRST. Bolt on the lever-7 template recovery in the same day for near-zero marginal cost: take the ~50-80 VSX RCB stars and known multi-year eclipsers at G<=16.5 in footprint and confirm the Gaia-present/ZTF-absent pipeline recovers the ones in 2018-2026 minima on its own configuration -- if it cannot recover its own positives, nothing downstream means anything.
biggest_risk: The lane spends 2-4 weeks building an elaborate, genuinely well-designed ZTF-reference forensics apparatus to reconstruct a measurement that ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2 has already made, openly, for every single Tier-0 target -- and then finds that the handful of survivors are either already in VSX/Gaia Alerts (vetoed out by its own gates) or are the 0-2 residual objects that the ASAS-SN team's next magnitude slice will sweep up with better photometry and a publication the user cannot match. Secondary risk, near-certain and cheap to fix: the missing bright cut makes the stated FP funnel wrong by ~30x, so the first real run returns ~1e6 raw non-matches instead of 3e4 and the "one week" Tier 0 becomes a month of deblending forensics. Tertiary: the classification bottleneck. A 4.5-mag 8-year fade with no spectrum is fileable to VSX as UNIQUE or RCB:, so credit is NOT telescope-gated, but the scientifically interesting distinction (RCB vs dust-cocooned post-AGB vs long eclipse) is, which caps what the named consumers (Tisserand, Kenworthy, VASCO) can do with a handout.
one_line_reason: Technically the best-constructed lane I have gated -- real controls, a stop rule, per-quadrant coverage proof, a legitimate escape from the closed turn-on lane's structural trap, and every data endpoint verified public -- but its founding claim that these objects are invisible by construction is false: ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2 serves open, reference-independent, nightly light curves for 98.6M REFCAT2 stars at g<18.5, a superset of the entire Tier-0 sample over the exact fade window, so the population is already measured and merely un-flagged in one magnitude slice the incumbent is visibly walking toward, which drops the honest novel yield from 2-10 to 0-2 for 2-4 weeks of work.

prior_art_found:
Found on every sub-branch, and one of the hits is a MEASURED NULL of this lane's own method.

BRANCH 1 (astrometric veto on non-thermal "AGN" catalogues):
1. arXiv:2301.08010 ran exactly this on SRG/eROSITA: sources classified extragalactic that have significant Gaia PM. Result: 502 such sources, of which only ~1.5% are actually Galactic stars; the rest are extended optical sources / astrometric artifacts. The companion paper arXiv:2309.11308 shows near-nuclear transients manufacture spurious PM. So the veto has been run on the flagship X-ray dataset and the measured yield of genuinely-Galactic novelties was ~7 objects out of 2M, essentially all already known.
2. The premise "88% of eRASS hard-band counterparts were never astrometrically checked" is FALSE. eROSITA DR2 (A&A aa60385-26, 2026) ships NWAY counterparts against Gaia DR3 + LS10 + CatWISE2020 as part of the release; eRASS1 already has a dedicated counterpart-identification-and-classification paper (Salvato+2025, A&A aa56142-25) plus HamStar (arXiv:2401.17282), a dedicated run to pull the Galactic coronal content out of the same catalogue. Galactic/extragalactic separation using Gaia is the release's own product, not a gap.
3. The 4FGL sub-branch (spiders inside bcu/unassociated) is an active professional industry: arXiv:2412.11616 systematically period-searched ZTF light curves around 2,157 4FGL-DR3 unassociated sources, then cut on Gaia HRD position, 95% ellipse containment and reduced proper motion — this lane's exact recipe, already executed and published. Plus COBIPLANE (ApJ, 10.3847/1538-4357/ae313f), COBIPULSE, arXiv:2411.16350 (4FGL J1544.2-2554), and a large BCU-classification ML literature.
4. Quasar-catalogue cleaning: CatNorth (arXiv:2310.12704), CatSouth (arXiv:2503.14141), Quaia, Gaia DR3 vari-AGN all apply astrometric filters. True, they do not publish the rejects — but the cut is loose (PM > 14 mas/yr, parallax > 6 mas) and the reject pile is millions of ordinary stars, not a hidden exotic sample.

BRANCH 2 (radio stars / WD+M):
5. Pelisoli+2024 (MNRAS 531, 1805 / arXiv:2402.11015): 846,000 Gaia WD candidates × VLASS E1. Pelisoli+2025 (arXiv:2505.04693): targeted Gaia+WISE binary-WD-pulsar search. Lane concedes both.
6. RACS-low2 Stokes I+V is public (RACS VIII, arXiv:2606.16182, Jun 2026) — and the RACS team itself published the star crossmatch within ~2 weeks (ATNF daily picture, 2026-07-03): 61 unique stars/systems, 67 measurements. The unidentified Stokes V tail is single-digit and the survey team gets it on release day.
7. LPT systematic searches are running from the radio side at scale: LoTSS DR2 Stokes V transient search (de Ruiter/Callingham), ASKAP EMU 10-s imaging (arXiv:2511.09770), Sherman+2025, Lee+2026.

Genuinely NOT found after 12 searches: a published crossmatch of a large WDMS/PCEB catalogue (Li+2025 Gaia-XP, or SDSS/LAMOST WDMS) against RACS-low2 Stokes V / LoTSS DR2 with an M-dwarf-dominated selection. That one narrow slice appears open.

scooped_fraction_estimate: ~80-90% overall. Branch 1 gamma-ray sub-branch ~90-95% scooped (2412.11616 + COBIPLANE + COBIPULSE run the identical ZTF-period + Gaia-astrometry recipe with telescope follow-up). why_not_done_claim_credible:
Mostly SELF-SERVING, with one honest sentence and one verifiable strength.

Self-serving / factually wrong:
- "The Fermi-LAT team never vetoes with Gaia astrometry" — technically true of the catalogue pipeline, but irrelevant: the whole downstream BCU/unassociated community does exactly that, systematically, and publishes it (arXiv:2412.11616 applies Gaia HRD + 95%-ellipse + reduced-PM cuts to 2,157 unassociated sources). Citing the catalogue team's pipeline while ignoring the dozen groups mining its output is the classic self-serving framing.
- "88%-'extragalactic' eRASS:3 hard-band counterparts" as unexamined territory — flatly contradicted by the DR2 release itself (NWAY vs Gaia DR3) plus Salvato+2025 and HamStar. This is the lane's weakest claim and it is the one carrying the largest claimed yield.
- "Flesch, Storey-Fisher and Fu applied PM cuts and threw the rejects away" — true and useless. The rejects are millions of ordinary stars at PM > 14 mas/yr; discarded does not mean unexamined-and-interesting.
- The AR Sco anecdote is pure survivorship bias: AR Sco sits in the Stern blazar WISE box, yes — and AR Sco is one of the most famous variable stars of the last decade. An example chosen because it is known cannot evidence a population that is unknown.

Honest:
- "Radio-first groups find pulses then look for counterparts, never starting from WD+M lists" — this is true and is the lane's only real opening. Pelisoli's reverse searches do structurally miss M-dwarf-dominated PCEBs.

Verifiable strength (credit where due):
- The "new supply" claim checks out: RACS-low2 Stokes I/V public Jun 2026 (arXiv:2606.16182), eROSITA-DE DR2 public 2026-07-31 (1,911,744 point sources), 5XMM-DR15 Jun 2026. The lane does say what changed, so it is not a bare recycle.
depth_arithmetic:
BRANCH 2 — RADIO DEPTH (the binding constraint).
RACS-low2 rms 195 uJy/beam -> 5-sigma ~ 0.98 mJy. AR Sco: 5-9 mJy at parallax 8.54 mas (d = 117 pc). Flux ~ d^-2, so horizon d_max = 117 x sqrt(7/0.98) = 117 x 2.67 = ~310 pc.
Volume to 310 pc = 1.25e8 pc^3; RACS covers dec <= +48 deg = ~0.75 of sky -> 9.3e7 pc^3 accessible.
The lane's own cited theory (arXiv:2604.18688) puts 100-1,000 such systems within 2 kpc. Sphere at 2 kpc = 3.35e10 pc^3 -> density 3e-9 to 3e-8 pc^-3. In the accessible 9.3e7 pc^3 that is 0.3 to 2.8 objects TOTAL, before beaming fraction, before duty cycle, before the fact that RACS is a snapshot survey.
Empirical confirmation of that arithmetic: Pritchard's ~100 circularly polarised RACS-mid sources contained exactly ONE object with no ID within 10 arcsec (ASKAP J1745-5051). The RACS team crossmatched RACS-low2 Stokes V against known stars within ~2 weeks of release and got 61 identified systems. So the genuinely unidentified polarised tail this lane would work is single-digit and already picked over by the people who built the catalogue. "Expected 0-3 objects" in the lane text is honest; what it omits is that the competitors have the same 0-3 objects, earlier, with ATCA and spectroscopy.

BRANCH 1 — GAMMA-RAY ASSOCIATION ARITHMETIC (shows the veto does not select).
4FGL-DR4 typical 95% ellipse semi-major ~4-8 arcmin. At r = 5 arcmin, area = 0.0218 deg^2. Gaia DR3 source density at |b| = 20-40 deg is ~2e4 deg^-2 -> ~440 Gaia sources PER ELLIPSE. Across 1,625 bcu that is ~7e5 Gaia sources inside association regions, well over half with 5-sigma PM. So "veto = parallax or PM at >=5 sigma on counterparts within the association radius" returns ~3.5e5 chance-coincident stars, not a shortlist. It only works on the single named counterpart.
Restricted to named counterparts (1,625 bcu + ~2,300 bll/fsrq = ~3,900): Gaia detects maybe 50-70% at G = 17-21 -> ~2,400 with astrometry. For a real AGN at G ~ 19-20, sigma_parallax = 0.3-1.0 mas, so 5-sigma requires parallax > 1.5-5 mas, i.e. d < 200-670 pc. Any Galactic non-thermal emitter that close and that bright is already catalogued. Expected genuinely-new: ~0-3, not the claimed 5-30.
Scale check on the big tables: Gaia DR3 qso_candidates is 6.6M rows at ~52% purity, i.e. ~3.2M non-quasars that are predominantly stars. A 5-sigma PM cut on that returns of order 1e6 rows. Assef R90 (4.5M) behaves similarly. These are not "100-200 vettings at 10 min each" — they are population-sized triage problems, and the 10-min-per-object budget in the lane text is off by 3-4 orders of magnitude at the input stage.

BRANCH 1 — X-RAY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED.
arXiv:2301.08010 already did the veto on eROSITA: 502 "extragalactic" sources with significant Gaia PM, of which ~1.5% (~7 objects) are actual Galactic stars, the rest extended/artifact. Scaling that hit rate to eRASS:3's 1,911,744 point sources does not help, because the false-positive channel scales with the sample while the true positives are already in SIMBAD.

cheapest_kill_test:
Run the veto on a labelled control where the answer is already published, and measure the funnel instead of assuming it. Concretely, one afternoon, two TAP queries, zero new code:

Apply the exact proposed cut (Gaia DR3 parallax OR PM at >= 5 sigma) to the eRASS1 counterparts that Salvato+2025 classified as extragalactic, then split the survivors three ways: (a) already SIMBAD/VSX-classified Galactic, (b) astrometrically spurious (RUWE > 1.4, or LS10-extended, or the near-nuclear-transient signature of arXiv:2309.11308), (c) genuinely uncatalogued and astrometrically clean. arXiv:2301.08010 predicts bucket (c) is ~1.5% of survivors and that essentially all of it lands in (a) once cross-checked. If (c) comes out below ~10 objects across the whole eRASS1 extragalactic sample, branch 1 has no funnel and dies the same afternoon — and this test also satisfies lever 7, because it recovers a known answer on the pipeline's own configuration before any absence claim is made.

One-hour companion that kills branch 2 independently: count how many RACS-low2 Stokes V sources have NO SIMBAD/Gaia identification within 10 arcsec. Pritchard's RACS-mid answer was 1 out of ~100, and the RACS team published its own RACS-low2 star crossmatch on 2026-07-03. If the unidentified count is <= 5, the entire branch-2 supply is <= 5 objects and they belong to the people who took the data.
biggest_risk:
The astrometric veto is satisfied by artifacts, not by astrophysics — and this is the exact structural failure that already closed the turn-on lane ("deep-sharp vs shallow-coarse comparison is definitionally satisfied by blends, sub-threshold noise, cosmic rays").

Here the mechanism is documented rather than hypothetical: faint AGN counterparts with host structure, near-nuclear transients, blends and marginal astrometric solutions produce 5-sigma parallaxes and proper motions that are not real (arXiv:2309.11308). When the cut was actually applied to eROSITA, 502 sources passed and ~98.5% were NOT Galactic stars (arXiv:2301.08010). So the survivor list is an artifact catalogue with a thin dusting of already-known stars, and every survivor costs a ~10-minute human vetting. A 100-200 object vetting budget against a funnel with a ~1.5% true-positive rate and a true-positive population that is ~100% already catalogued is a machine for manufacturing confident nulls out of pipeline noise.

Secondary risk, specific to the one open corner: branch 2B's load-bearing input (Li+2025 Gaia-XP WDMS) has unverified public availability, and its 0-3 expected objects are the same 0-3 objects the RACS/LOFAR teams reach first with their own data and follow-up time.
one_line_reason: The lane's core method has already been run and published on the flagship dataset with a measured near-null (502 PM-significant eROSITA "extragalactic" sources, ~1.5% genuinely Galactic and those already catalogued), eROSITA DR2 ships its own Gaia-based counterpart classification plus HamStar so the "88% unexamined" premise is false, the 4FGL side is occupied by active ZTF-period + Gaia-astrometry spider pipelines with telescope follow-up, and the one genuinely open corner (WDMS x RACS-low2 Stokes V) is bounded by depth arithmetic at 0-3 objects within ~310 pc that the survey teams crossmatch within two weeks of release.

Branch B (RCB via 2MASS-vs-Gaia optical deficit) is KILLED by prior art the lane misrepresents. scooped_fraction_estimate: ~60-70% of the bundle is scooped or structurally dead. Branch B: ~95% scooped (Tisserand 2194 all-sky + Karambelkar PGIR triage + Gaia DR3 153 covers the RCB/DYPer parent regardless of decline epoch). Branch A: ~40% scooped in method (2MASS-vs-later-NIR difference already used for PM by the UHS team and for variability vs VHS), but the specific fade-direction cut at |b|>5 against UHS K/H is genuinely un-run. Branch C: ~20% scooped -- the excluded-middle wedge is documented and open, but the interesting sub-populations (symbiotics) are being actively harvested by better-equipped groups.
why_not_done_claim_credible: Mixed, and self-serving where it matters most. CREDIBLE: the UHS timing argument (K public 2023-06, H public 2025-09-17, so a 2MASS-vs-UHS-K/H epoch difference has a ~12-month-old substrate); the UHS team's published science really is brown dwarfs, high-PM objects and quasars, not variability; the PGIR census cuts really do exclude 0.5-2 mag events by construction -- I verified that claim against the paper's own abstract. SELF-SERVING: the RCB defence ("every channel needs the decline inside its own window") is simply wrong for Tisserand's dust-shell colour selection, which is epoch-independent and all-sky -- the proposal needed to address that and did not. Also omitted entirely: the |b|<5 restriction of Contreras Pena/Lucas/VVV is not an oversight by those teams, it is where the eruptive-YSO and symbiotic populations LIVE. Moving to |b|>5 does not open an unworked field; it moves to a field where the target objects are largely absent. The proposal presents a population constraint as a prior-art gap.
depth_arithmetic:
MEASURED, not assumed. Queries run live this session against IRSA TAP and NOIRLab Data Lab TAP (both anonymous, both returned real rows).

BRANCH A (fade direction) -- depth PASSES with margin. 2MASS 10-sigma limits J=15.8 / H=15.1 / Ks=14.3 (Vega). UHS 5-sigma medians J~19.6, H=19.0, K~18.0-18.4. A Ks=12.5 star fading 2.5 mag lands at Ks=15.0, which is ~3.0-3.4 mag above the UHS K limit. Headroom is real. Parent sample MEASURED: 2MASS fp_psc with dec 0-60, |b|>5, k_m<12.5, ph_qual A = 7,082,046 rows. UHS covers 12,700 deg^2 at dec 0-60 minus prior UKIDSS footprints, so ~3-4M of those are usable.
BRANCH A (turn-on direction) -- FAILS on dynamic range. WFCAM/UHS nominal saturation is ~11 mag and UHS explicitly flags and EXCLUDES saturated photometry from band-merged relations. So the usable turn-on window is only K ~11.0 to 14.3 (2MASS limit) = 3.3 mag, and anything that brightened past K=11 is unmeasurable in the very survey meant to detect it. The lane never mentions saturation.
BRANCH A coverage: UHS = dec 0 to +60 ONLY. The southern half depends entirely on VHS at the VSA, which I could NOT reach (vsa.roe.ac.uk returned connection failure 000 on three attempts; surveys.roe.ac.uk/vsa/ 302-redirects into the same dead host). So ~half the claimed sky is access-unverified.
BRANCH A yield reality: the lane claims 20-30% odds of a FUor-class object, but FUors are accretion outbursts of embedded YSOs and therefore concentrate at |b|<5; the |b|>5 star-forming clouds (Taurus, Oph, Perseus, Cham, Lupus) are small in area and among the most heavily Spitzer/Herschel/ZTF/PGIR/WISE-monitored sky there is. The lane's own symbiotic-slow-nova rate (~3 per half-century, plane-concentrated) gives an expectation well under 1 event in a 12,700 deg^2 northern cap over 1997-2024. Dominant contaminant: 2MASS is a SINGLE epoch, so a Mira with dK=1.5-2 mag caught near maximum in 1998 and near minimum in a 2017-24 UHS scan manufactures a >=2.5 mag "fade" with no astrophysical novelty, and there are order 1e5 such stars at Ks<12.5.

BRANCH C -- parent sample is far smaller than the pitch implies. PGIR: dec>-28, ~18,000 deg^2, 8.7 arcsec/pixel, J_AB <~13 in-plane and <~15 out-of-plane = J_Vega <~12.1 / <~14.1; ~70M sources in reference images. DR1 light curves are seeded from 2MASS (I confirmed the Data Lab schema: pgir_dr1.sources carries pts_key, tmcra, tmcdec, tmcjmag, tmchmag, psfcontam) -- which is a genuine plus for selecting optically-dark 2MASS stars, but it caps the search at what 2MASS saw. MEASURED parent for "extremely red, |b|>5, dec>-28, ph_qual A": J-Ks>2.0 and J<12.5 = 6,830 objects; J<13.5 = 11,812; J<14.5 = 29,994. Only the J<~12.5 end has the SNR for reliable 0.5-mag detection through an 8.7-arcsec pixel. So the real working sample is ~7e3 objects, not the 1e4 shortlist the pitch implies from a 149M-row table -- and J-Ks>2 at J<12.5 is the classic dusty-AGB locus, so the large majority are already-catalogued Miras/SRs/carbon stars. The 0.5-2 mag "excluded middle" in that sample is, astrophysically, ordinary AGB pulsation.

BRANCH B -- no depth problem, a statistics problem. The cut is a 2.5-mag residual of Gaia G against a G(J-Ks) prediction over an ~3e8-source parent. The intrinsic scatter of that relation across mixed dwarfs/giants/metallicities/binaries/patchy extinction is >=0.3-0.5 mag in the core with a fat non-Gaussian tail (carbon stars, blends, bad 2MASS photometry, AGB variability between the 2000 and 2015 epochs). A 2.5-mag cut will return ~1e4-1e5 outliers, not the "~1e3-scale vetting" claimed, and they will be dominated by exactly the dust/extinction degeneracy the branch is trying to exploit.

cheapest_kill_test:
ONE-DAY CONTAMINANT-DENSITY TEST ON A SINGLE UHS DEC STRIP -- run Branch A fade-only and nothing else, because it is the only sub-branch with both correct depth arithmetic and an unworked cut.

One WSA freeform SQL job on a ~200 deg^2 strip (dec 20-25, |b|>5): 2MASS Ks<12.5, ph_qual A in K, cc_flg='0', prox clean, XSC-excluded, Gaia DR3 PM-propagated to the 2MASS scan epoch, joined to uhsSource; keep sources >=2.5 mag fainter in K or absent in all available UHS bands. Then, on the survivors only: (a) drop anything with a Gaia DR3 vari_classifier / LPV flag, (b) drop anything with a VSX or SIMBAD match, (c) drop anything with unTimely W1 peak-to-peak >0.3 mag over 2010-2020 (the Mira-caught-at-max killer -- a single-epoch 2MASS anchor cannot distinguish a fade from a pulsation minimum, and this is the dominant contaminant). Same job must ALSO recover, on the identical pipeline configuration, the known large-amplitude IR variables that fall in the strip (lever 7 -- no absence claim without template recovery).

DECISION RULE, fixed before running: extrapolate surviving density to the 12,700 deg^2 UHS footprint. If the projection is <10 all-sky survivors, or if >90% of survivors fail the unTimely-flat test, or if the known-variable recovery is incomplete, the lane dies that day. Cost: one SQL job, one crossmatch, one unTimely pull. This single number also decides Branch C, because if the bright red 2MASS sky is already fully catalogued as AGB variables then the PGIR excluded middle is new Miras, not new knowledge. Do NOT spend a day on Branch B -- it is already dead on Tisserand.
biggest_risk: The confident deliverable is bookkeeping, not novelty -- which is the one thing the objective rules out. Strip away the optimistic tails and what this lane reliably produces is newly-registered Miras, semiregulars and dusty AGB stars: VSX-gradeable, named-credit, and explicitly not new-to-knowledge. The claimed novel yields all sit on weak legs: FUors and symbiotics concentrate at |b|<5 and the lane deliberately works |b|>5; the symbiotic slow-nova rate the lane itself quotes (~3 per half-century) gives an expectation well under 1 in the accessible footprint; and Branch B's RCBs are already enumerated all-sky by Tisserand and PGIR-triaged by Karambelkar. Second-order but severe: 2MASS is a SINGLE epoch, so every "state change" in Branch A is a two-point inference in which a pulsation minimum is indistinguishable from a decade-long fade -- the whole lane rests on unTimely mid-IR flatness as its only discriminator, and Miras are 0.5-1 mag variable in W1, so that discriminator is doing far more work than the proposal acknowledges. Third: this partially recycles the closed turn-on lane. The fade direction genuinely escapes the "sub-threshold noise" failure (the 2MASS anchor is SNR~30, not a noise-floor NSC detection) -- that is a real and defensible change -- but the proposal never identifies it, which means the design was not built with that lesson in hand and the turn-on direction still walks straight into it, on top of the unmentioned UHS ~11 mag saturation ceiling.
one_line_reason: Branch B is dead on prior art the lane misdescribes (Tisserand's 2194 colour-selected RCBs are epoch-independent and already PGIR-triaged by Karambelkar+2024) and Branch C's real wedge yields mostly new Miras from a measured parent of only ~6,830 objects, but Branch A's fade-only cut has verified anonymous access, ~3 mag of genuine UHS depth headroom over a measured 7.08M-source high-SNR 2MASS anchor, and an un-run 12-month-old substrate -- so it earns exactly one day of contaminant-density testing, not a two-week three-branch campaign.
